    mapi_spec¶

    This package has contracts that use only Pydantic. It does not use numpy, xarray or pandas, because the control plane depends on this package.

    Data schema¶

    Data contract primitives: dims, variables, ragged structure and dataset schemas.

    A :class:DataSchema describes an xr.Dataset without any arrays: its dims (each with a :class:DimPolicy saying what may happen to it at score time), its variables (with a :class:Role, dtype, units and missingness) and its ragged structure.

    A :class:DataSchemaTemplate is a static JSON function of enumerated settings: plugins export one per model so the control plane can compute the required input schema for given settings without running plugin code.

    DimPolicy ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    What may happen to a dim's coordinates at score time.

    FIXED ¶

    FIXED = 'fixed'

    Score coords must be a subset of fit coords (channel, state, product).

    EXTEND ¶

    EXTEND = 'extend'

    New coords may be appended after the fit range, contiguously (time, obs).

    NEW_LEVELS ¶

    NEW_LEVELS = 'new_levels'

    Unseen levels are allowed through a declared strategy (market, county).

    DimSpec ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A dimension and its score-time policy.

    Role ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    What a variable means to a model.

    VarSpec ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A data variable: its dims (by name), dtype, role, units and missingness.

    RaggedSpec ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Ragged nesting (hh → trip): long form (obs + index vars) or padded + mask.

    DataSchema ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Schema of an xr.Dataset: dims, variables, layout and ragged structure.

    vars_with_role ¶

    vars_with_role(*roles: Role) -> list[str]

    renamed ¶

    DataSchemaTemplate ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A DataSchema-shaped JSON template plus the settings parameters it depends on.

    Resolution is pure and static: resolve(settings) extracts each declared parameter from the settings (falling back to its default), checks its type/enum, renders the :mod:~mapi_spec.template placeholders, deep-merges every matching case and validates the result as a :class:DataSchema.

    A constant template (no parameters).

    Documents¶

    Declarative documents: ModelSpec, ScoreRequest and the wrapper kinds.

    Every document has apiVersion: mapi/v1 and a kind discriminator. All models forbid unknown fields. See :mod:mapi_spec.loader for strict parsing and canonical hashing and :mod:mapi_spec.validate for static validation against a catalog.

    The declarative modelling file.

    Bases: StrictModel

    Names that are not bound keep their dataset name. The binding is stored in the bundle and reversed on every output by default.

    settings.dim_policies is platform-reserved: a mapping dim → policy that may only tighten the plugin's policies. It is removed before plugin settings validation.

    Loading and hashing¶

    Strict YAML 1.2 / JSON loading, apiVersion upgrades, canonical JSON and spec hashing.

    The loader is safe for hostile input:

    • size ≤ 256 KB, nesting depth ≤ 32, ≤ 10 000 nodes (all configurable via :class:Limits);
    • YAML anchors, aliases, explicit tags (!foo, !!python/...), %TAG directives and multiple documents are rejected;
    • plain scalars are resolved with the YAML 1.2 core schema (yes/on/0777/dates stay strings), NaN/Infinity are rejected, duplicate keys are rejected and every mapping key must be a string;
    • JSON input is parsed with the same limits.

    :func:load_document returns a typed document (discriminated on kind) after running the apiVersion upgrade chain (the API accepts N and N-1). :func:canonical_json and :func:spec_hash give a normalised, deterministic serialisation for immutable revisions.

    Limits ¶

    Limits(
    max_bytes: int = 256 * 1024,
    max_depth: int = 32,
    max_nodes: int = 10000,
    max_scalar_bytes: int = 64 * 1024,
)

    Parser limits for untrusted documents.

    load_document(
    text: str | bytes, limits: Limits = DEFAULT_LIMITS
) -> Any

    Parse YAML/JSON text and validate it as a typed document.

) -> ModelSpec

    parse_document(

    canonical_json ¶

    canonical_json(obj: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any]) -> str

    Deterministic JSON: defaults omitted, keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8, ints for integral floats. Equal documents (after normalisation) produce identical text.

    spec_hash ¶

    spec_hash(obj: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any]) -> str

    sha256:<hex> of the canonical JSON (the immutable revision identity).

    Capabilities, manifests and outputs¶

    Model capabilities, uncertainty representations and the model manifest.

    The :class:Representation of a model's output decides which aggregations and summaries are statistically valid. Those rules live here as data (:data:REPRESENTATION_RULES) and small functions (:func:can_aggregate, :func:summary_allowed) so the control plane, the runner summariser and the UI all agree.

    Representation ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    How a model encodes uncertainty in its outputs.

    DRAWS ¶

    DRAWS = 'draws'

    (chain, draw, *dims) joint samples — any aggregation is valid.

    QUANTILES ¶

    QUANTILES = 'quantiles'

    (quantile, *dims) marginal quantiles — no cross-cell aggregation.

    INTERVAL ¶

    INTERVAL = 'interval'

    (bound, *dims) + alpha, e.g. conformal — no aggregation.

    POINT ¶

    POINT = 'point'

    (*dims) point predictions — linear aggregation only, flagged.

    MOMENTS ¶

    MOMENTS = 'moments'

    (moment=[mean, sd], *dims) e.g. analytic GP — per-cell only.

    Capabilities ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    What a model plugin can do (declared in its manifest).

    ModelManifest ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Everything the control plane knows about a model plugin version (static JSON).

    model_family ¶

    model_family: str

    family or, when unset, the id's namespace (ts.sarimax -> ts).

    OutputDecl ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    An output variable the model writes (e.g. y_hat).

    full_dims ¶

    full_dims(schema: DataSchema | None) -> list[str]

    dims plus the dims of dims_of in the model's resolved input schema.

    DerivedDecl ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A derived quantity (contributions, response curves, ...).

    OutputSelector ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    What a score request returns.

    summary_for ¶

    summary_for(rep: Representation) -> list[str]

    The requested summary, or the representation default if none was given.

    Aggregation ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Reduce outputs over dims before summarising (validity depends on representation).

    Diagnostic ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A diagnostic finding that rolls up into the sanity scorecard.

    can_aggregate ¶

    can_aggregate(
    rep: Representation,
    over_dims: list[str] | tuple[str, ...],
    how: str = "sum",
) -> AggregationVerdict

    Is reducing an output over over_dims with how statistically valid?

    summary_allowed ¶

    summary_allowed(rep: Representation, name: str) -> bool

    Whether summary name can be computed from output in representation rep.

    default_summary ¶

    default_summary(rep: Representation) -> list[str]

    The default summary list for a representation.

    parse_summary ¶

    parse_summary(name: str) -> ParsedSummary

    Parse a summary name. Raises ValueError for unknown names.

    Schema effects and stages¶

    Step kinds, SchemaEffects, context needs and static schema propagation.

    A :class:SchemaEffect is a data-free description of how a preprocessing step changes a :class:~mapi_spec.schema.DataSchema. Step authors export it as JSON (per image digest); the control plane evaluates it with :func:propagate and never imports step code.

    Effects may be templates: strings can reference the step's settings with the :mod:~mapi_spec.template placeholder syntax ("{dim}", "{*vars as v}"). Every referenced setting must be listed in template_params. :func:resolve_effect renders a template with concrete settings into a plain :class:SchemaEffect.

    Within one effect, operations apply in this order: renames → drops → transforms_dims → stacks → unstacks → updates → derives → adds.

    StepKind ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    RESHAPE changes structure (not invertible past it); VALUE rescales; FEATURE adds.

    SchemaEffect ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    How a step changes the schema. See the module docstring for ordering rules.

    ContextNeed ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Per-group tail a step needs at score time: n rows along along within groups.

    min_lag is the smallest lag the step applies (for recursive-forecast checks); it defaults to 1 when the step depends on the target.

    Stage ¶

    Stage(name: str, schema: DataSchema | None)

    The dataset schema after a step (name = step id; raw before any step).

    propagate ¶

    propagate(
    raw_schema: DataSchema,
    steps: Sequence[
        tuple[str, EffectInput, Mapping[str, Any]]
    ],
    *,
    pointer_base: str = "/pipeline",
    pointers: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> PropagationResult

    Propagate raw_schema through steps = [(step_id, effect, settings), ...].

    Effects may be templates; settings are substituted into them. A dynamic effect stops static propagation: that stage and every later one are None and a SCHEMA_DYNAMIC warning is reported (an explicit dry-run can resolve it).

    resolve_effect ¶

    resolve_effect(
    raw: SchemaEffect | Mapping[str, JsonValue],
    settings: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> SchemaEffect

    Render a templated effect with concrete settings.

    Raises :class:~mapi_spec.template.TemplateError or pydantic.ValidationError.

    apply_effect ¶

    apply_effect(
    schema: DataSchema, effect: SchemaEffect
) -> tuple[DataSchema | None, list[str]]

    Apply one resolved effect. Returns the new schema (or None) and problems.

    Static validation¶

    Static (JSON-only) validation of ModelSpecs and ScoreRequests.

    :func:validate_spec checks a :class:~mapi_spec.spec.ModelSpec against a :class:~mapi_spec.catalog.Catalog and the dataset's raw :class:DataSchema:

    1. binding references exist and do not collide;
    2. every use: resolves to a non-yanked version (semver range);
    3. step and model settings validate against their JSON Schemas;
    4. side-table references exist;
    5. the schema is propagated through every step's SchemaEffect, with per-step input checks;
    6. the split stage is resolved (default: end of the stateless prefix), its dims exist there, and LEAKAGE_RISK is raised if a stateful step precedes it;
    7. the model's schema template is resolved and compared with the final stage; spec dim policies may only tighten the plugin's;
    8. recursive forecasting (a target-dependent lag feeding a longer holdout) is rejected unless the model owns recursion; outputs, plots, metrics and resource class are checked.

    :func:validate_score_request runs the static CoordPlan checks for a ScoreRequest from metadata only (resolved spec + fit coordinate summaries + dim policies).

    Every finding is an :class:~mapi_spec.errors.Issue with a JSON pointer into the document.

    SpecValidation ¶

    SpecValidation(
    issues: list[Issue],
    stages: list[Stage],
    resolved: ResolvedSpec | None = None,
)

    Outcome of :func:validate_spec.

    ResolvedSpec ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    What the control plane stores with a run: everything score-time checks need.

    last_reshape_stage ¶

    last_reshape_stage: str

    Inverse transforms stop here (the output space of results).

    steps_after ¶

    steps_after(stage: str) -> list[ResolvedStep]

    Steps executed when data enters at stage.

    ScoreMetadata ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Per-model-version metadata used for static CoordPlan checks.

    fit_coords maps a stage name to coordinate summaries of the full fit data at that stage (the production refit), at least for the model stage.

    validate_spec ¶

    validate_spec(
    spec: ModelSpec,
    catalog: Catalog,
    raw_schema: DataSchema,
) -> SpecValidation

    Statically validate spec against catalog and the dataset's raw_schema.

    validate_score_request ¶

    validate_score_request(
    req: ScoreRequest,
    meta: ScoreMetadata,
    inputs: DataSummary | None = None,
    *,
    max_draws: int | None = None,
    live_capabilities: Capabilities | None = None,
) -> list[Issue]

    Static CoordPlan checks for req against a fitted model's metadata.

    inputs summarises the payload (data or scenario) as it enters at req.inputs_stage; dataset names are mapped through the binding at every stage, as the runtime does. When it says where the targets hold values (inputs.observed), a forecast's actuals are checked (:mod:mapi_spec.actuals). live_capabilities are those of the plugin build that will score, which may have gained score-time features (conditions_on_actuals) since the fit; the fitted ones are used otherwise.

    Catalogs¶

    Static catalog entries for steps, models and plots (exported per image digest).

    The control plane validates specs against these JSON shapes only — it never imports the step or model code that produced them.

    Catalog ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A set of catalog entries with semver resolution helpers.

    resolve_step(ref: UseRef | str) -> StepCatalogEntry | None

    See :func:catalog_about_issues.

    StepCatalogEntry ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Everything static validation needs to know about one step version.

    effect and context are JSON templates over the step's settings (see :mod:mapi_spec.template). var_params/dim_params name settings fields whose values are variable/dim names that must exist at the step's input stage, and side_table_params name fields that refer to data.side_tables entries.

    ModelCatalogEntry ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A model plugin version: its manifest plus registry metadata.

    about ¶

    about: About | None

    The manifest's About card (M3.5).

    PlotCatalogEntry ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A plot recipe the runner can produce.

    catalog_about_issues ¶

    catalog_about_issues(
    catalog: Catalog,
    *,
    extra_ids: Iterable[str] = (),
    builtins: bool = True,
) -> list[Issue]

    The catalog rule (M3.5): an ABOUT_INCOMPLETE error for every non-yanked step and model of catalog whose About is missing or incomplete (:func:mapi_spec.about.about_issues), and a warning for each related id that names no known item, located by JSON pointers into the catalog document.

    Known ids are the catalog's own, extra_ids and (builtins) every built-in card's id (:func:mapi_spec.abouts.builtin_abouts: splits, templates, workflow nodes, checks).

    Errors¶

    Stable error codes, RFC 7807 problem documents and the MapiError hierarchy.

    Every error the platform returns carries a stable machine-readable code (one of :class:ErrorCode). Codes never change meaning once released; new codes are additive.

    Untrusted text (tracebacks, user-supplied values echoed back, plugin messages) is always carried in a separate untrusted_text field and never merged into detail/message.

    ErrorCode ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Stable error codes. See :data:ERROR_INFO for HTTP status and titles.

    MapiError ¶

    MapiError(
    detail: str,
    *,
    code: ErrorCode | None = None,
    pointer: str = "",
    untrusted_text: str | None = None,
    issues: Sequence[Issue] = (),
)

    Bases: Exception

    Base exception: carries a stable code, a JSON pointer and optional untrusted text.

    Bases: BaseModel

    One problem found while validating a document, located by a JSON pointer.

    Problem ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    RFC 7807 problem document with mapi extensions (code, errors, untrusted_text).

    Severity ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    How bad an :class:Issue is. Only error blocks submission.

    ValidationFailed(
    issues: Sequence[Issue], detail: str | None = None

    Static validation produced at least one error; issues holds them all.

    Plot envelope¶

    The PlotSpec envelope: a Vega-Lite or Plotly spec plus named datasets and provenance.

    Datasets are referenced by name only (Vega-Lite data: {name: ...}, Plotly {"$ref": "name.column"}) and never by URL. The full plot sanitiser (schema validation, HTML stripping, URL rejection everywhere) lives in mapi_plots; this module enforces the envelope contract: shapes, name references and the no-URL data rule.

    PlotSpec ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A renderable plot. spec is Vega-Lite JSON or Plotly {data, layout, ...}.

    InlineArrow ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A small Arrow IPC stream embedded as base64.

    DataRef ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A dataset stored next to the bundle (path relative to the bundle root).

    PlotBindings ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Role/dim template bindings, e.g. {x: "dim:time", y: "role:target"}.

    Templates bound this way apply to every model of a family, not one bundle.

    PlotProvenance ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Who produced a plot: exactly one of recipe, plugin or author.

    Executor protocol¶

    mapi_spec.run exports the executor shapes again with no changes.

    Executor protocol shapes (plan §8.4), shared by the control plane and the runtimes.

    The control plane drives every backend (in-process, local process, docker, Cloud Run Jobs, ...) through one :class:Executor protocol. Identifiers travel in the environment only; the executor's status API is the liveness source of truth and events are advisory progress. These are pure Pydantic shapes: no numpy, xarray or plugin code.

    Executor ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    A backend driver. Identifiers reach the run through the environment only.

    RunSubmit ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    One attempt of a run, as handed to an executor (JSON only).

    RunKind ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    What a run does. validate is the explicit sandboxed dry-run of a spec.

    sweep, backtest, sbc and campaign are fan-out parents (plan §6.2, M4): they own child runs and never execute on an executor themselves.

    TRANSLATE_PRIORS ¶

    TRANSLATE_PRIORS = 'translate_priors'

    M3: business priors → model-space priors plus a prior-predictive preview in business units (sandboxed; :class:mapi_spec.calibration.PriorTranslationJob).

    Run protocol¶

    For the full description, read Run protocol.

    The run protocol (plan §8.1, §8.3–§8.7): state machine, bootstrap, events, manifests.

    Everything a control plane, an executor and a runner must agree on lives here, as pure Pydantic / stdlib code:

    • :class:RunState, :class:RunTrigger and the transition table :data:TRANSITIONS, with the pure function :func:transition used by the API, dispatcher, events service, reconciler, finalizer and tests;
    • :class:RunSpec — the bootstrap object written to bootstrap/<nonce> before an execution starts (signed URLs, a per-run HMAC key, limits, deadline);
    • :class:~mapi_spec.executor.RunEvent payload models, canonical HMAC-SHA256 signing and verification, and the stdout JSONL wire format ({"mapi_event": {...}} per line);
    • :class:OutputManifest (the runner's claim), metadata-only verification against server-computed hashes, and the platform-signed :class:BundleManifest;
    • the runner invocation contract: environment (:class:RunnerEnv) and exit codes (:class:RunnerExit).

    Executor-facing shapes (:class:Isolation, :class:ExecutorCaps, :class:Handle, :class:ExecStatus, :class:RunKind, :class:RunEvent, ...) are defined in :mod:mapi_spec.executor and re-exported here unchanged, so both import paths name the same classes.

    Job payloads¶

    See Job payloads and object names.

    Run job payloads: what RunSpec.spec holds for each run kind, plus the input and output object names shared by the control plane (which writes RunSpecs and reads outputs) and the runner (which reads RunSpecs and writes outputs).

    ========== ============================================ ====================================== kind RunSpec.spec inputs (RunSpec.inputs names) ========== ============================================ ====================================== ingest :class:IngestJob (a bare IngestMapping upload (the raw file; dataset is also accepted) is accepted as a fallback) describe :class:DescribeJob none validate a ModelSpec document dataset, optional schema, side.<name> fit a ModelSpec document dataset, optional schema, side.<name> score a ScoreRequest document, or bundle, optional :class:ScoreJob bundle.manifest, dataset (the request's data), scenario, side.<name>, history (M3: the fit dataset, for carry_last / seasonal_naive future covariates) evaluate :class:EvaluateJob bundle, dataset, ... derive :class:DeriveJob bundle, dataset, side.<name> render :class:RenderJob plots (a plots.json) translate_ :class:~mapi_spec.calibration.Prior- ``dataset``, optional ``schema``, priors TranslationJob (M3) side.<name>; output priors.json workflow_ :class:~mapi_spec.workflow.WorkflowNode- ``in.<port>.<k>`` (each bound input); node Job (M3.5) output node_result.json explore :class:~mapi_spec.explore.ExploreJob dataset (+ schema) or (M3.5) bundle, bundle.manifest, compare.<k>; output ui/explore/ optimize :class:~mapi_spec.optimize.OptimizeJob bundle, bundle.manifest; output (M3.5) optimize.json governance :class:~mapi_spec.governance.Governance- ``bundle``, ``bundle.manifest``, Job (M3.5) dataset, optional evaluation (+ evaluation.manifest); output governance.json ========== ============================================ ======================================

    workflow runs are parents (the orchestrator walks the DAG) and never execute.

    Datasets are single-object *.zarr.zip files. A dataset's raw schema comes from the schema input, else the zarr root attribute mapi_schema (written by ingest), else it is inferred. bundle is the bundle.zarr.zip of a fit and bundle.manifest the SDK bundle manifest that the fit uploaded as bundle.manifest.json.

    This module is pure Pydantic (no numpy/xarray): the control plane imports it.

    IngestJob ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    An ingest run: an explicit column mapping, or the MFF preset.

    From M3 the mapping itself may name a preset (mapping.preset: mff or meridian, with its options in the mapping); the top-level preset/mff pair stays for v0.2 callers.

    IngestSource ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    What the uploader declared about the raw file (informational; never trusted).

    MffOptions ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    The MFF ("model feature format") long-table preset.

    One row per (period, geography, product, campaign, outlet, creative, variable) with the value in value_column. Period becomes the time dim; VariableName values become data variables. The rest follows mmm-framework's MFF semantics (its MFFLoader), so both read a file the same way:

    • Geography and Product become dims when they hold more than one level. A blank label (or National, Total, All) is the coarser level: a variable given only there (national TV) is spread across the levels - equal weights, or the KPI's share of each level (allocation; mmm-framework's defaults: geographies equally, products by sales). A variable may not mix the two levels.
    • Campaign, Outlet and Creative are breakdowns: rows that differ only there are summed, unless the column is listed in split (then it becomes a dim).

    combine joins several key columns into one dim ({"geo": ["Geography", "Product"]} gives labels such as US|Watches) - a model with one panel dim can then fit a geography x product panel. A combined dim is created even when it has a single label, so {"geo": ["Geography"]} keeps a national table's geo dim.

    UI views¶

    Precomputed UI views: small JSON documents the runner writes next to datasets and bundles and the browser reads through signed URLs (the control plane never decodes them).

    Every view carries a format tag so readers can refuse versions they do not understand:

    ===================== ======================== ========================================== file format content ===================== ======================== ========================================== preview.json mapi.preview/v1 a long-format sample: dim then var columns profile.json mapi.profile/v1 per-variable statistics + missingness grid ui/tree_index.json mapi.tree-index/v1 structure of the bundle DataTree (no arrays) ui/preprocess.json mapi.preprocess/v1 learned preprocessing state per pipeline step ui/grids/mapi.response-grid/v1per-draw response curves for what-if sliders response_curves.json (M3; :class:ResponseGridView) ui/guided/mapi.forecast/v1a forecast score run's KPI: history, then the forecast.json forecast fan after the split (M3) ui/guided/mapi.counterfactual/v1a counterfactual score run's change of the counterfactual.json KPI, in total and per period (M3) ui/explore/mapi.model-explorer. quantised posterior rasters of the outputs fields.jsonfields/v1 that declare a grid (:class:FieldsView) ===================== ======================== ==========================================

    Views are produced inside the sandbox from untrusted data: strings are capped and readers must render them as text only.

    Object storage¶

    Object storage contracts (plan §8.6): metadata, the ObjectStore protocol, signed URLs, integrity hashes and the bucket/key naming scheme.

    The control plane talks to object storage only through :class:ObjectStore. Two implementations exist outside this package: ShimObjectStore (the local GCS emulator in mapi_gcs_shim) and GcsObjectStore (google-cloud-storage). Both expose GCS semantics:

    • every write creates a new generation; if_generation_match=0 means "only if the object does not exist" (write-once);
    • the server computes CRC32C (base64 of the big-endian 4-byte value) and MD5 (base64 of the 16-byte digest) — uploader-supplied hashes are never evidence;
    • signed GET URLs are pinned to a generation and honour HTTP Range; signed PUT URLs and V4 POST policies (key prefix + content-length-range) are how sandboxes write, so the executor never holds storage credentials.

    Object keys are always built server-side from validated IDs with the helpers at the bottom of this module (never from user-supplied paths).

    ObjectStore ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    Async object-store driver used by the control plane (GCS semantics).

    Conventions shared by every method:

    • generation pins the source generation to read (None = live generation);
    • if_generation_match is a precondition on the target: 0 means "must not exist", n means "live generation must be n"; a failed precondition raises :class:PreconditionFailed;
    • missing buckets/objects raise :class:NotFound; denied operations raise :class:AccessDenied.

    V4 POST policy allowing uploads of any key under prefix within the size range.

    create_only uploads may not replace an existing object (whatever the signer's own permissions).

    ObjectMeta ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Metadata-only view of one object generation (what objects.get returns).

    crc32c and md5_hash are computed by the storage service, never by the uploader. md5_hash is absent for composite objects (GCS semantics).

    from_gcs_resource ¶

    from_gcs_resource(
    resource: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> ObjectMeta

    Build from a GCS JSON-API object resource (generation/size are strings).

    to_gcs_resource ¶

    to_gcs_resource() -> dict[str, Any]

    The GCS JSON-API shape (inverse of :meth:from_gcs_resource).

    same_content ¶

    same_content(other: ObjectMeta) -> bool

    Size and server-computed hashes agree (generation and location may differ).

    ObjectPage ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    One page of :meth:ObjectStore.list.

    SignedGet ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A generation-pinned signed GET URL plus the server-computed facts about its object.

    The URL honours HTTP Range, so zarr zip readers can range-read one object. A reader verifies size/crc32c after a full download (corruption check only — integrity is enforced by the control plane).

    SignedPut ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A signed PUT URL for exactly one object name.

    headers must be sent verbatim (they are part of the signature): typically content-type, x-goog-if-generation-match: 0 (write-once) and x-goog-content-length-range: 0,<max_bytes>.

    PostPolicy ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A V4 POST policy: multipart form uploads of any key under prefix.

    The uploader posts multipart/form-data to url with every entry of fields, then key (which must start with prefix), then the file part last. The storage service rejects bodies outside content_length_range and keys outside the prefix.

    A create_only policy cannot replace an existing object (its signed conditions carry x-goog-if-generation-match: 0), so the holder can neither overwrite the write-once manifest nor swap an output after it was written.

    allows ¶

    allows(key: str, size: int) -> bool

    Whether an upload of size bytes to key satisfies this policy.

    REST DTOs¶

    For the endpoint tables and the conventions, read HTTP API (v1). Also read the multi-tenant additions of v0.3.

    REST DTOs for the HTTP API (/v1; plan §8.2): M1 (v0.2), M2 (v0.3) and the M3 (v0.4) contracts.

    Conventions shared by every endpoint (see docs/reference/http-api.md):

    • Requests reject unknown fields (extra="forbid"); responses ignore unknown fields when parsed by a client, so older clients keep working when the server adds fields.
    • Every resource carries tenant_id and project_id. M1 is single-tenant: both are :data:DEFAULT_TENANT_ID / :data:DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID, but the identity is in every row and key so M2 can add row-level security without migrations churn.
    • Lists return :class:Page (items + opaque next_cursor); errors are RFC 7807 :class:~mapi_spec.errors.Problem documents with stable codes.
    • Timestamps are timezone-aware RFC 3339 strings in UTC.

    :data:M1_ENDPOINTS, :data:M2_ENDPOINTS (v0.3), :data:M3_ENDPOINTS (guided mode and integrations, v0.4) and :data:M35_ENDPOINTS (workflows, governance, explorers, optimisation and About cards, v0.5) are the machine-readable endpoint tables; :data:ENDPOINTS (= :data:ALL_ENDPOINTS) is all four. The server's route table and the reference docs are tested against them. :data:ROUTE_ACCESS gives every operation its tenant/project scope and the permission it checks. From v0.3 every M1 resource is project-scoped: the project comes from the path or the X-Mapi-Project header (:func:mapi_spec.tenancy.resolve_project_scope).

    Tenant/project scoping and the permission checked for every operation in :data:ALL_ENDPOINTS (keyed by operation_id; M3.5 rows from :data:_M35_ACCESS).

    Acting on other principals' tokens (list_tokens?all=true, revoking someone else's token) additionally needs manage on token. A create_run for a model version (score, evaluate, derive, render) additionally needs run on model. A promote_endpoint with override=true additionally needs manage on endpoint, which no token scope grants (a signed-in admin decides, audited with the reason).

    Page ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel, Generic[T]

    One page of a list endpoint. Pass next_cursor back as ?cursor= for the next page; None means this is the last page. ?limit= defaults to 50 (max 200).

    Dataset ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    DatasetCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Create an (empty) dataset; data arrives as versions.

    UploadCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Ask for a signed PUT URL into the quarantine bucket for one file.

    UploadSession ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Where to PUT the file. upload.headers must be sent verbatim; the URL expires.

    IngestMapping ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    How an upload becomes a labelled dataset (Meridian CoordToColumns style).

    Tabular formats need a mapping; zarr_zip/netcdf are self-describing and may omit dims/vars. Parsing happens only inside a sandboxed ingest run.

    With the mff preset the long table is first pivoted to one column per VariableName (plus Period and the key columns); vars and wide then pick and rename those variables (column = a VariableName value) and dims may refine the dims the preset derives (column = an MFF column). Without vars and wide every variable is kept under its own name.

    effective_mff ¶

    effective_mff: MffOptions | None

    The MFF options the ingest run uses (defaults for the mff preset).

    DimMapping ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    A dim of the dataset, read from one column of a tabular upload.

    VarMapping ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    A data variable read from one column (dtype is inferred during ingest).

    DatasetVersionCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Turn a finished upload into a new version via a sandboxed ingest run (202).

    DatasetVersion ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    An immutable, content-addressed version (data.zarr.zip + schema + profile).

    DatasetVersionStatus ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    SpecCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Create a spec document with its first revision (YAML 1.2 or JSON text).

    SpecDoc ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A named spec and its latest revision.

    SpecRevisionCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Add an immutable revision. parent_revision guards against lost updates (409).

    SpecRevision ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    One immutable, canonically hashed revision. issues holds its static validation.

    ValidateRequest ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Synchronous static validation of a document (exactly one of yaml/document).

    dataset overrides the dataset version whose stored schema is the raw input schema (default: the spec's own data.dataset reference, resolved now).

    ValidateResponse ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Every problem at once, located by JSON pointers, plus per-stage schemas.

    StageSchema ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    The data schema after one pipeline step (raw = after binding, before any step).

    RunCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Submit a run. Send an Idempotency-Key header: a retry with the same key and body returns the original run (200); the same key with a different body is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Keys are scoped to the project and kept for 24 h.

    • fit / validate (sandboxed dry-run): spec_id + revision;
    • score: model_version_id + request;
    • evaluate / derive / render: model_version_id (+ params).

    RunRetry ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /runs/{id}:retry: a new run from a failed one, optionally one class up.

    Run ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A unit of work and its lifecycle (see the state machine in mapi_spec.run).

    ProgressSnapshot ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Latest coalesced progress (one upserted row per run).

    RunEventView ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A persisted run event (id is the SSE event id, increasing per run).

    LogLine ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    One captured line. line is untrusted text: render it as text only.

    SseEventName ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    event: names on GET /v1/runs/{id}/events (text/event-stream).

    snapshot (the full :class:Run, no id) is sent first on every connection; run-event types carry id: = :attr:RunEventView.id; end is sent once the run is terminal, then the server closes the stream.

    Model ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A registry entry grouping the versions fitted from one spec name.

    ModelVersion ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A verified bundle: signed manifest, diagnostics, scorecard, lineage and metrics.

    Scorecard ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Sanity scorecard: convergence, holdout error and plausibility checks rolled up.

    ScorecardItem ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Lineage ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Everything a model version came from (plan §8.6).

    ScoreCall ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Body of POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}:score.

    Send Prefer: wait=N (N ≤ 60) to wait for the result: the response is 200 with outputs if the run finished in time, else 202 with the run (poll it or follow its SSE). inline carries data/scenario typed in instead of named as datasets; the request then names neither.

    ScoreCallResult ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    done with output links (200), or the still-running run (202). summary is the requested summary (mean and HDI by default) inline, once the run succeeded.

    ArtifactLink ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A short-lived, generation-pinned signed GET URL for one artifact (HTTP Range works).

    ObjectRef ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A stored object exposed through …/artifacts/{name} (fetch it as an ArtifactLink).

    PlotListItem ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A plot available for a model version; fetch the sanitized :class:PlotSpec at href.

    PlotValidateResponse ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Result of POST /v1/plots:validate (the server-side plot sanitizer).

    CatalogResponse ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    The static catalog the control plane validates against (no plugin code involved).

    Health ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    /healthz (process liveness) and /readyz (dependencies) body.

    HealthCheck ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Me ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    GET /v1/me: who the caller is and where they may act.

    For a token, tenants holds exactly the token's project and token the token itself (its scopes narrow every role shown here).

    MeTenant ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A tenant the caller belongs to; role is the tenant-wide role (None when the caller only has project memberships).

    MeProject ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A project the caller can act in, with the caller's effective role there.

    TenantCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /v1/admin/tenants (operators). initial_admin_email is invited as tenant admin; the invitation is claimed at first login with that verified e-mail.

    TenantUpdate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id} (tenant admins): the display name only.

    TenantAdminUpdate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Tenancy and authorization¶

    See Tenancy and authentication.

    Tenants, projects, roles, principals and authorization (plan §2, §8.1, §9).

    • A tenant is the billing, isolation and quota boundary, with a :class:TrustTier that decides where its runs may be placed (:func:placement_allows) and a data-residency region (:func:region_satisfies).
    • A project is a workspace inside a tenant and the RBAC unit. Roles are ordered viewer < editor < runner < admin: editors change datasets and specs, runners may also spend compute (runs, scores), admins manage members, endpoints and plugins.
    • :data:PERMISSIONS is the whole permission matrix; :func:can is the pure check every component uses. :class:AuthContext combines it with token scopes, tenant status and the operator flag (:meth:AuthContext.allows).
    • :func:resolve_project_scope turns the X-Mapi-Project header, path parameters and a token's binding into the (tenant, project) a request acts in.

    Pure Pydantic and stdlib: the server, the web app (through OpenAPI) and tests share it.

    *,

    parse_project_selector ¶

    parse_project_selector(value: str) -> ProjectSelector

    Parse "<tenant>/<project>" or "<project>" (raises SCHEMA_INVALID).

    resolve_project_scope ¶

    resolve_project_scope(
    *,
    header: str | None = None,
    path_tenant: str | None = None,
    path_project: str | None = None,
    token_binding: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
    member_tenants: Collection[str] = (),
    default: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
) -> ProjectSelector

    Decide which (tenant, project) a project-scoped request acts in.

    Precedence: path parameters, then the X-Mapi-Project header, then the token's binding, then default (the single-tenant deployment profile only).

    • path and header that disagree → SCHEMA_INVALID;
    • a token used outside its binding → FORBIDDEN (tokens are bound to one project);
    • a bare project id is qualified with the path tenant, the token's tenant, or the only tenant the principal belongs to; otherwise → SCHEMA_INVALID;
    • nothing selects a project and there is no default → SCHEMA_INVALID.

    Membership is checked afterwards; a project the caller cannot see is NOT_FOUND (not FORBIDDEN), so ids cannot be probed.

    API tokens¶

    API tokens: wire format, scopes, at-rest hashing and the token DTOs (plan §8.2, §9).

    Token format (all lowercase Crockford base32, 0-9a-z without i l o u)::

    mapi_<prefix>_<secret><checksum>
     8 chars  32 chars 7 chars
    • prefix (40 random bits) is public: it is shown in listings and is the lookup key;
    • secret (160 random bits) is shown exactly once, in :class:TokenCreated;
    • checksum is the CRC-32 of mapi_<prefix>_<secret> (ASCII) in 7 base32 digits, so clients and secret scanners can reject typos and random strings without a database call.

    At rest the server stores only :func:hash_token of the whole token (HMAC-SHA256 under a server-side pepper) and compares with :func:verify_token_hash in constant time. No API response ever contains the hash or, after creation, the secret.

    A token acts as its owner, narrowed by its scopes: every request needs both the owner's project role (:func:mapi_spec.tenancy.can) and a scope that covers the action (:func:scope_allows). Tokens are bound to one project of one tenant.

    No scope covers :data:TOKEN_NEVER: minting tokens (a child token would escape its parent's expiry, budget, rate limit and revocation), overriding a promotion gate and approving a model validation (human decisions that are audited) need a signed-in session.

    Sessions and Pub/Sub push¶

    Authentication protocols shared by the server and the web app (plan §8.1, §8.7, §11).

    Browser sessions (BFF). The SPA never sees an OAuth token. GET /auth/login starts an OpenID Connect Authorization Code flow with PKCE (S256) and a nonce; the transaction is kept server-side, referenced by a short-lived __Host- cookie. GET /auth/callback checks state, exchanges the code, verifies the ID token (issuer, audience, nonce, expiry) and sets the session cookie: HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ with no Domain. Because the cookie is SameSite=Strict and every state-changing endpoint takes JSON (a CORS-preflighted content type), cross-site requests never carry it.

    Programs send Authorization: Bearer mapi_… (see :mod:mapi_spec.tokens).

    Pub/Sub push to POST /internal/events carries a Google-signed OIDC ID token; after verifying the signature, the server checks its claims with :func:check_push_claims.

    Server-side state of one login between /auth/login and /auth/callback.

    Quotas and scheduling¶

    See Quotas and cost.

    Quotas, rate limits, priority classes and fair-share leasing (plan §8.3, §8.8, §9).

    Three levels of :class:QuotaPolicy apply to every request and run, most specific first: token, tenant, global. Each sets optional :class:QuotaLimits (None = unlimited at that level). :func:evaluate_quota is the single pure decision function: the first limit a demand would exceed yields a :class:QuotaDecision with problem code RATE_LIMITED (request rate; retryable) or QUOTA_EXCEEDED (everything else).

    Quotas are expressed in vCPU-seconds because abuse risk is compute, not run count. :class:PriorityClass weights drive :func:plan_leases, the dispatcher's weighted fair-share choice of which queued runs to lease next, so one tenant's 237-task SBC cannot starve everyone else's interactive scoring.

    evaluate_quota ¶

    evaluate_quota(
    levels: Iterable[tuple[QuotaPolicy, QuotaUsage]],
    demand: QuotaDemand,
    *,
    now: datetime,
) -> QuotaDecision

    Check demand against every level; return the first violation or an allowance.

    Order: request rate at every level first (RATE_LIMITED), then per level from token to global (QUOTA_EXCEEDED): resource class, fan-out width, concurrent runs, vCPU-seconds per day and month, storage, egress. A cumulative limit fails when used + requested > limit and only if the demand asks for some of it, so a subject already over its storage quota can still read and delete. retry_after_seconds is set for windowed limits (minute, UTC day, UTC month).

    plan_leases ¶

    plan_leases(
    candidates: Sequence[LeaseCandidate],
    *,
    capacity: int,
    running_tasks: Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    concurrency_left: Mapping[str, int | None]
    | None = None,
    tenant_weights: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    weights: Mapping[
        PriorityClass, float
    ] = PRIORITY_WEIGHTS,
) -> list[LeaseCandidate]

    Choose which queued runs to lease now (weighted fair share; pure and deterministic).

    Repeatedly picks the candidate with the smallest virtual finish (load[tenant] + tasks) / (tenant_weight × priority_weight), ties broken by queued_at then run_id. load starts at the tenant's running_tasks and grows with every pick. A candidate is skipped when its tasks exceed the remaining global capacity or its tenant has no concurrency_left (runs). Returns the picks in order.

    backoff_seconds ¶

    backoff_seconds(
    attempt: int,
    *,
    base: float = 1.0,
    cap: float = 64.0,
    retry_after: float | None = None,
) -> float

    Delay before retry attempt (1-based) after a 429: min(cap, base·2^(attempt-1)), never shorter than a server-sent Retry-After. Callers add jitter.

    Cost¶

    Price tables, cost estimates and the per-run cost ledger (plan §8.2, §13 cost floor, §14 M2).

    Money is integer micros of a currency (1 USD = 1,000,000 micros); unit prices are integer nanos per vCPU-second and per GiB-second, so every amount is exact and reproducible from a ledger row (round half to even at the micro). Every amount names the :class:PriceTable version it was priced with; changing prices never rewrites history.

    Usage of an attempt is vcpu × billed_seconds × tasks vCPU-seconds and ram_gib × billed_seconds × tasks GiB-seconds, from :data:RESOURCE_CLASSES; billed_seconds is wall time rounded up to the table's billing increment.

    :data:DEFAULT_PRICE_TABLE mirrors Cloud Run's published list prices (CPU 0.000018 USD per vCPU-second, memory 0.000002 USD per GiB-second); deployments configure their own. An E33 fit on class M for five minutes costs about 0.03 USD.

)

    Audit¶

    Audit events: who did what to which resource, and whether it worked (plan §9, §11 Admin).

    Audit rows are append-only. They identify actors by platform id, never by e-mail, and never store raw client IPs or user agents: :func:client_fingerprint keys an HMAC with a deployment secret, so rows can be correlated ("same address as before") without being reversible. Secrets (token values, signed URLs) never appear in details.

    Operator controls¶

    Operator controls: kill switches and executor health (plan §9 denial of wallet, §11 Admin).

    :class:KillSwitches is a single platform-wide document. :func:kill_switch_decision is the pure check the API (at submit) and the dispatcher (at lease) both apply: when untrusted_execution_enabled is off, no run of uploaded (tenant) code is accepted or leased; when the global spend in the current window reaches global_spend_cap_micros, no new compute is accepted for anyone except internal tenants. Both denials use the QUOTA_EXCEEDED problem code at the global scope.

    Executor conformance suite¶

    The executor conformance suite, as data (plan §8.4, §13 "Executor conformance").

    An executor (local-process, docker, docker-gvisor, cloudrun-jobs, ...) is enabled only after it passes every applicable case of :data:EXECUTOR_CONFORMANCE. Each :class:ConformanceCase names the behaviour, the fault the harness injects, what the backend must support for the case to apply, and the :class:Expectation on the run's observed trajectory. The server's pytest suite parametrizes over this tuple and checks each observation with :func:check_expectation; the admin API reports results as a :class:ConformanceReport.

    EXECUTOR_CONFORMANCE ¶

    EXECUTOR_CONFORMANCE: Final[tuple[ConformanceCase, ...]] = (
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.SUBMIT,
        title="Submit runs one execution to success",
        behaviour="A submitted attempt starts with identifiers in the environment only, reports status through the executor API, emits verified events and succeeds.",
        steps=(
            "submit a tiny fit with a fresh nonce",
            "poll status until terminal; collect events",
            "assert argv carries no run id, nonce or credential",
        ),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(
                _S.PROVISIONING,
                _S.RUNNING,
                _S.FINALIZING,
            ),
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.1", "§8.3", "§8.4"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.ADOPT_AFTER_DISPATCHER_CRASH,
        title="Orphan adoption after a dispatcher crash",
        behaviour="If the dispatcher dies between the executor accepting an attempt and the handle being stored, the reconciler adopts the execution by nonce instead of starting a second one.",
        steps=(
            "write the intent row, submit, crash before storing the handle",
            "restart the orchestrator; reconciler calls adopt(nonce)",
            "the adopted execution finishes the run",
        ),
        fault=Fault.DISPATCHER_CRASH_AFTER_SUBMIT,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.DUPLICATE_SUBMIT,
        title="Duplicate submit is safe",
        behaviour="Submitting the same (run, attempt, nonce) twice never yields two live executions; the second call returns or adopts the first, or its execution is cancelled before it does any work.",
        steps=(
            "submit twice with the same nonce",
            "wait for the run to finish",
        ),
        fault=Fault.DUPLICATE_SUBMIT,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            attempts=1,
            max_live_executions=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.CANCEL_MID_RUN,
        title="Cancel while running",
        behaviour="A cancel during RUNNING moves the run to CANCELLING; the supervisor gets SIGTERM and flushes; the run is CANCELLED only after the executor confirms the execution is gone.",
        steps=(
            "submit a long fit; wait for RUNNING",
            "cancel; poll executor status",
            "assert CANCELLED is recorded after the executor reports a terminal state",
        ),
        fault=Fault.CANCEL_WHILE_RUNNING,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.CANCELLED,
            must_visit=(_S.RUNNING, _S.CANCELLING),
            must_not_visit=(_S.SUCCEEDED, _S.FAILED),
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§8.7"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.TIMEOUT,
        title="Timeout is enforced and classified",
        behaviour="A run that exceeds its timeout is stopped by the backend (hard task timeout as backstop) and ends FAILED with failure class timeout.",
        steps=(
            "submit a run that sleeps past a short timeout",
            "wait for the run to end",
        ),
        fault=Fault.EXCEED_TIMEOUT,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.FAILED,
            failure_class=FailureClass.TIMEOUT,
            attempts=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§8.7"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.STALLED_NOT_LOST,
        title="Event silence raises STALLED, never a false LOST",
        behaviour="When events stop but the executor still reports the execution running, the run becomes STALLED (a warning) and returns to RUNNING when events resume; it is never failed or retried because of silence alone.",
        steps=(
            "submit; drop events beyond K x interval while the execution runs",
            "resume events; let the run finish",
        ),
        fault=Fault.EVENT_SILENCE,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(_S.STALLED,),
            must_not_visit=(_S.FAILED,),
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "Key decisions: liveness"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.CONFIRMED_CANCEL_BEFORE_RETRY,
        title="Confirmed cancel before an infrastructure retry",
        behaviour="After an infrastructure failure the reconciler cancels the old execution and waits for a confirmed terminal status before re-queueing attempt + 1, so two attempts never run at once.",
        steps=(
            "submit; report an infra failure while the old execution is alive",
            "observe cancel → confirmed terminal → QUEUED(attempt 2)",
            "attempt 2 succeeds",
        ),
        fault=Fault.INFRA_FAILURE_LIVE_EXECUTION,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(_S.QUEUED,),
            attempts=2,
            max_live_executions=1,
            executions_created=2,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.CHECKPOINT_RESUME,
        title="Checkpoint, PARTIAL and resume",
        behaviour="A SIGTERM after checkpoints were written yields a PARTIAL bundle; resume starts a new attempt from the checkpoints and completes without redoing them.",
        steps=(
            "submit a segmented fit; wait for the first checkpoint",
            "SIGTERM the execution; expect PARTIAL",
            "resume; expect SUCCEEDED with the earlier segments reused",
        ),
        fault=Fault.SIGTERM_WITH_CHECKPOINTS,
        requires=frozenset(
            {Requirement.CHECKPOINT_STORAGE}
        ),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(_S.PARTIAL,),
            attempts=2,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§5 segmented sampling"),
        budget_seconds=300,
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.OOM_CLASSIFICATION,
        title="Out-of-memory is classified as resource exhaustion",
        behaviour="A worker killed for memory (exit 137) ends FAILED with failure class resource_exhausted and an offer to retry one class up.",
        steps=(
            "submit a memory bomb at class S",
            "wait for the run to end",
        ),
        fault=Fault.MEMORY_BOMB,
        requires=frozenset({Requirement.MEMORY_LIMIT}),

    ConformanceCase(

        behaviour="One execution with task_count N runs N tasks, each mapping its task index to a child spec and writing under tasks/{i}/; status aggregates all tasks and a cancel stops all of them.",
        steps=(
            "submit task_count=4",
            "assert 4 distinct task indexes and per-task output prefixes",
            "assert one backend execution",

    Guided mode v0.4¶

    See Guided mode.

    Guided mode: templates, the question flow, role detection and drafts (plan §11; M3).

    Guided mode is organised around tasks. The user picks a :class:GuidedTemplate ("What do you want to learn?"), answers plain-language :class:GuidedQuestion s about their columns ("Which column is revenue?") - pre-filled by :func:suggest_roles from column profiles - and gets a draft: an :class:~mapi_spec.ingest.IngestMapping for the upload plus a ModelSpec document (and its YAML, "View as YAML"), built by :func:build_draft.

    Templates are data. Their spec_template is a ModelSpec document with {{placeholder}} strings, filled from answers, template defaults and lookups (:func:render_template); every placeholder is covered by a question, a default, a lookup or a value the builder always provides (:data:BUILDER_VALUES), which a test checks.

    Built-in templates (:data:GUIDED_TEMPLATES):

    ================= ========================== ============================================= id plugin for ================= ========================== ============================================= geo_mmm mmm.bayesian marketing mix by market (what-if, priors; mmm-framework's BayesianMMM) weekly_forecast````ts.hsgp_trend one weekly series, forecast ahead store_demand tabular.regressor demand per store and week (quantiles) customer_choice````choice.multinomial_logitwhich product customers choose on each trip (a conditional logit with household effects, in plugins/tabular) ================= ========================== =============================================

    GUIDED_TEMPLATES ¶

    GUIDED_TEMPLATES: Final[dict[str, GuidedTemplate]] = {
    t.id: t.model_copy(
        update={"about": TEMPLATE_ABOUTS[t.id]}
    )
    for t in (
        GEO_MMM,
        WEEKLY_FORECAST,
        STORE_DEMAND,
        CUSTOMER_CHOICE,
    )
}

    The built-in guided templates, by id (GET /v1/guided/templates).

    GuidedTemplate ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A guided task: questions, the spec they fill and what to check afterwards.

    ui_levels maps JSON pointers of the spec to x-ui-level hints (hidden fields are kept but not shown; Expert edits round-trip). plugin_available is false while the template's built-in plugin is not shipped (plugin_note says what is missing).

    GuidedQuestion ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    One plain-language question. Column questions name what the column becomes:

    • dim: the column labels a dataset dim (dim_spec describes it); the placeholder {{<id>}} is the dataset dim name;
    • role (column): the column is a data variable with that role; the placeholder is the dataset variable name;
    • role + wide_dim (columns): the columns become one variable as_var along wide_dim (one label per column, e.g. spend per channel);
    • role without wide_dim (columns): each column is its own variable.

    TemplateLookup ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A placeholder derived from an answer: map[answer] (e.g. frequency → season).

    ColumnProfile ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    What the browser (DuckDB-WASM/papaparse preview) or an ingest profile knows about a column. name and sample are user data: render them as text only.

    DetectRolesRequest ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /v1/guided/detect-roles: exactly one of dataset (a stored version: its schema and profile are used) or columns (profiled in the browser).

    RoleCandidate ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    QuestionSuggestion ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Candidates for one question (best first) and the pre-filled answer.

    RoleSuggestions ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    GuidedAnswers ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /v1/guided/drafts: answers to a template's questions.

    Column answers are column names of the upload (a list for columns questions). dataset names the dataset the upload will become (dataset://<project>/<name>); columns (optional) lets the draft use detected types and frequencies.

    GuidedDraft ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    The draft a template and its answers produce: how to ingest the upload, the spec, the spec as YAML ("View as YAML") and anything worth a second look.

    get_template ¶

    get_template(template_id: str) -> GuidedTemplate

    A built-in template (NOT_FOUND otherwise).

    template_placeholders ¶

    template_placeholders(obj: Any) -> set[str]

    Every {{name}} in a template (keys and values).

    render_template ¶

    render_template(obj: Any, values: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any

    Fill {{name}} placeholders: a string that is only a placeholder becomes the value itself (any JSON); placeholders inside longer strings are replaced by the value's text. Raises KeyError for a placeholder without a value.

    suggest_roles ¶

    suggest_roles(
    template: GuidedTemplate,
    columns: Sequence[ColumnProfile],
) -> RoleSuggestions

    Rank columns for every column question and pre-fill answers (pure heuristics).

    Single-column questions take the best column at confidence ≥ 0.5 not used by an earlier question; multi-column questions take every remaining column at ≥ 0.5. frequency is answered from the chosen date column's detected frequency.

    build_draft ¶

    build_draft(
    template: GuidedTemplate,
    answers: GuidedAnswers,
    *,
    project: str,
) -> GuidedDraft

    Turn answers into an ingest mapping and a ModelSpec (pure; validated).

    Raises GUIDED_ANSWERS_INVALID for a missing required answer, a column used twice, a choice or number out of range, or a resulting spec that does not parse.

    safe_name ¶

    safe_name(column: str) -> str

    A dataset name for a column (Revenue (EUR) → revenue_eur).

    channel_label ¶

    channel_label(
    column: str, noise: Sequence[str] = ()
) -> str

    A label from a wide column name (TV_Spend_EUR → tv): the name's words minus money and unit words and minus noise (the question's keywords, so price_coke and promo_coke both become coke).

    Ingest presets v0.4¶

    Ingest presets and file contracts (plan §3.2, §11 Guided task 2, Q8; M3).

    An upload becomes a labelled dataset in a sandboxed ingest run. Besides an explicit column mapping (:class:mapi_spec.api.IngestMapping), M3 adds presets for the formats marketing teams already have:

    ================= =========================================================================== preset file contract ================= =========================================================================== none the explicit dims/vars/wide column mapping mff the MFF long table (:data:MFF_COLUMNS): one row per period, key columns and variable, the value in VariableValue (:class:MffOptions) meridian Google Meridian's CoordToColumns wide table (:class:MeridianColumns) ================= ===========================================================================

    Wide tables (one column per channel) become one variable along a new dim through :class:WideVarMapping - the shape Meridian and most spreadsheets use.

    This module only describes files; every byte of an upload is parsed inside the sandbox.

    MFF_COLUMNS ¶

    MFF_COLUMNS: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = (
    "Period",
    "Geography",
    "Product",
    "Outlet",
    "Campaign",
    "Creative",
    "VariableValue",
    "VariableName",
)

    The MFF long-format columns, in the order of the MFF convention (and mmm-framework). Every row holds one value: VariableValue of variable VariableName for one Period and one combination of the key columns.

    MFF_KEY_COLUMNS ¶

    MFF_KEY_COLUMNS: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = (
    "Geography",
    "Product",
    "Outlet",
    "Campaign",
    "Creative",
)

    The MFF key columns besides Period (each becomes a dim when it has >1 value).

    IngestMapping ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    How an upload becomes a labelled dataset (Meridian CoordToColumns style).

    Tabular formats need a mapping; zarr_zip/netcdf are self-describing and may omit dims/vars. Parsing happens only inside a sandboxed ingest run.

    With the mff preset the long table is first pivoted to one column per VariableName (plus Period and the key columns); vars and wide then pick and rename those variables (column = a VariableName value) and dims may refine the dims the preset derives (column = an MFF column). Without vars and wide every variable is kept under its own name.

    effective_mff ¶

    effective_mff: MffOptions | None

    The MFF options the ingest run uses (defaults for the mff preset).

    DimMapping ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    A dim of the dataset, read from one column of a tabular upload.

    VarMapping ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    A data variable read from one column (dtype is inferred during ingest).

    WideVarMapping ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    One variable read from several columns, one per label of dim (a wide table).

    {"dim": "channel", "columns": {"tv": "tv_spend", "search": "search_spend"}} gives a variable along channel (plus the table's other dims) with coords tv and search. Several wide variables may share a dim; their labels must then agree.

    IngestPreset ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    MffOptions ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    The MFF ("model feature format") long-table preset.

    One row per (period, geography, product, campaign, outlet, creative, variable) with the value in value_column. Period becomes the time dim; VariableName values become data variables. The rest follows mmm-framework's MFF semantics (its MFFLoader), so both read a file the same way:

    • Geography and Product become dims when they hold more than one level. A blank label (or National, Total, All) is the coarser level: a variable given only there (national TV) is spread across the levels - equal weights, or the KPI's share of each level (allocation; mmm-framework's defaults: geographies equally, products by sales). A variable may not mix the two levels.
    • Campaign, Outlet and Creative are breakdowns: rows that differ only there are summed, unless the column is listed in split (then it becomes a dim).

    combine joins several key columns into one dim ({"geo": ["Geography", "Product"]} gives labels such as US|Watches) - a model with one panel dim can then fit a geography x product panel. A combined dim is created even when it has a single label, so {"geo": ["Geography"]} keeps a national table's geo dim.

    MeridianColumns ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Google Meridian's CoordToColumns contract for a wide CSV/Parquet table.

    media/media_spend (and reach/frequency/rf_spend) are parallel lists: the i-th column of each belongs to the i-th entry of media_channels (rf_channels). geo is omitted for a national model; kpi_type says whether the KPI is revenue (ROI in currency) or a count (revenue_per_kpi converts it).

    wide_vars ¶

    wide_vars() -> dict[str, WideVarMapping]

    The channel-indexed variables this contract defines (media, spend, reach, frequency, rf_spend), as :class:WideVarMapping along channel (rf_channel for reach and frequency).

    Business priors and calibration v0.4¶

    Business priors, lift tests and prior translation (plan §11 Guided task 3; M3).

    Guided users state beliefs in business units instead of model parameters:

    • :class:BusinessPriors - per channel an ROI range [low, high] or a contribution-share range, each held with a stated credibility (the probability that the truth lies inside the range), plus an optional baseline share;
    • :class:LiftTest - the result of an experiment (geo holdout, conversion lift): extra spend on one channel over a window and the incremental KPI it caused, with a standard error or a confidence interval. Lift tests are calibration data: the model treats each one as an extra observation of the channel's incremental effect.

    Both attach to a ModelSpec through its optional calibration block (:class:Calibration). A model plugin uses them only if its manifest declares the matching capability (Capabilities.calibration); otherwise static validation reports CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED.

    Turning business priors into model-space priors needs the data (spend and KPI scale) and the model's transforms, so it runs in the sandbox as a translate_priors run (:class:PriorTranslationJob → priors.json = :class:PriorTranslationResult), which also samples the prior predictive and reports it in business units (ROI and share distributions, a KPI fan). :func:apply_prior_translation writes the result into a spec.

    Pure Pydantic and stdlib (statistics.NormalDist for quantiles): the control plane and the web app (through OpenAPI) share it.

    BusinessPriors ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Beliefs in business units, per channel (keys are channel labels as in the data), and/or about the baseline. At least one belief is stated: a baseline belief alone is fine (channels without a belief keep the model's default priors).

    ChannelBelief ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    What the user believes about one channel: exactly one of roi or contribution_share, held with credibility.

    • roi: KPI units gained per spend unit over the fit window ([1.5, 4] = "every euro returns between 1.5 and 4 euros of revenue");
    • contribution_share: the channel's share of the KPI over the fit window.

    ShareBelief ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A share range (for example of the baseline: KPI that happens without any media).

    LiftTest ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    One experiment: spend_delta extra spend on channel (optionally in one geo) from start to end (inclusive) caused kpi_delta incremental KPI.

    Give the measurement's uncertainty as a standard error se or a confidence interval ci at ci_level. A holdout ("turn the channel off") is a negative spend_delta with (usually) a negative kpi_delta.

    sigma ¶

    sigma: float

    The standard error (from ci assuming a symmetric normal interval).

    implied_roi ¶

    implied_roi: float

    KPI gained per extra spend unit during the test.

    Calibration ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    The calibration block of a ModelSpec: beliefs and experiment results the model should respect. prior_translation_run records which translate_priors run produced the priors in model.settings.priors (lineage only).

    PriorTranslationJob ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    RunSpec.spec of a translate_priors run.

    spec is the resolved ModelSpec document (its data.dataset is the dataset input). The runner fits nothing: it builds the model, maps the beliefs to model-space priors and samples draws prior-predictive draws.

    PriorTranslationResult ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    priors.json of a translate_priors run.

    priors are model-space priors in the plugin's settings.priors form (engine-neutral {distribution, <params>, dims} dicts; per-channel parameters are lists in channels order), to be written at :data:PRIORS_POINTER. coverage is the prior mass inside each stated range (close to the stated credibility when the translation is faithful).

    PriorPreview ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    The prior predictive in business units: what the model believes before seeing the KPI, so users can check that their beliefs came out as intended.

    DistributionSummary ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A distribution in business units: mean, sd and named quantiles ("0.05" …).

    FanChart ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Quantile bands of a series along one dim (a KPI fan): values[i][j] is quantile quantiles[i] at coords[j]. observed (if any) is the data over coords.

    check_business_priors ¶

    check_business_priors(
    priors: BusinessPriors, pointer: str = ""
) -> list[Issue]

    Cross-field consistency of business priors (BUSINESS_PRIORS_INVALID issues).

    Shares cannot add up to more than the whole KPI: the lower bounds of every channel's share plus the baseline's must stay at or below 1. Upper bounds summing below 1 with a baseline belief leave KPI unexplained, which is a warning.

    lognormal_from_range ¶

    lognormal_from_range(
    low: float, high: float, credibility: float
) -> tuple[float, float]

    (mu, sigma) of the LogNormal whose central credibility interval is [low, high] (the translation of an ROI range). low must be positive.

    logitnormal_from_range ¶

    logitnormal_from_range(
    low: float, high: float, credibility: float
) -> tuple[float, float]

    (mu, sigma) of the logit-normal whose central credibility interval is [low, high] (the translation of a share range). Needs 0 < low < high < 1.

    apply_prior_translation ¶

    apply_prior_translation(
    document: dict[str, Any],
    result: PriorTranslationResult,
    *,
    business_priors: BusinessPriors | None = None,
    run_id: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]

    A copy of the ModelSpec document with result.priors merged into model.settings.priors (translated keys win) and the calibration block updated with business_priors and run_id (lineage).

    Scorecard and promotion gate v0.4¶

    The sanity scorecard and the promotion gate (plan §2 Diagnostic, §11 Guided task 5; M3).

    A fitted model version carries a :class:Scorecard: plain-language checks in four categories, each pass, warn or fail:

    ============== ========================================================================= category checks (:data:SCORECARD_CHECKS) ============== ========================================================================= convergence chains agree (R-hat), enough effective draws, no divergences holdout holdout error (MAPE) and interval coverage on the evaluation split; for choice models, the holdout hit rate against always guessing the most popular product plausibility negative or absurd ROI, a channel taking most of the KPI, the baseline share, parameters the data did not inform (prior-posterior overlap) data missing values, years of history, spend that never varies ============== =========================================================================

    :func:evaluate_check turns a metric value into a :class:ScorecardItem with the check's message and suggested action; :func:rollup makes the scorecard (overall is the worst item). Templates pick checks and may tighten thresholds (:class:CheckThresholds).

    Promoting a model version to an endpoint passes the promotion gate (:func:promotion_gate): pass → allowed, warn → needs an administrator override with a reason (audited), fail → blocked. :func:authorize_promotion applies an override request to a gate decision.

    items: Sequence[ScorecardItem],
    skipped: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
