    A scorecard whose overall is the worst item; with no item at all it is warn (nothing was checked).

    promotion_gate ¶

    promotion_gate(
    scorecard: Scorecard | None,
    *,
    fit_mode: str = "evaluate_then_refit",
    allow_train_only: bool = False,
    partial: bool = False,
    schema_breaks: Sequence[str] = (),
    schema_change: Literal[
        "block", "warn", "allow"
    ] = "block",
    required_checks: Sequence[str] = (),
    require_validated: bool = False,
    validation_status: str | None = None,
) -> PromotionGateDecision

    Decide whether a model version may be promoted (pure).

    M3.5: when a governance policy requires validation (require_validated, see :func:mapi_spec.governance.requires_validation), a version whose validation_status is not validated is blocked (NOT_VALIDATED): no override promotes it.

    • a partial version (interrupted fit) is blocked;
    • a train_only fit is blocked unless the endpoint's policy allows it (Q13: evaluate_then_refit is the default for endpoints, so context and terminal state come from all the data);
    • breaking input-schema changes (schema_breaks) follow schema_change;
    • no scorecard needs an override; a fail scorecard blocks, a warn one needs an override, a pass one is allowed;
    • an evaluate_then_refit version whose scorecard measured no holdout check (no data.split, or no evaluate.metrics) was never evaluated and needs an override (NOT_EVALUATED), as does every check of required_checks (a guided template's scorecard_checks) that the scorecard skipped or lacks.

    authorize_promotion ¶

    authorize_promotion(
    decision: PromotionGateDecision,
    *,
    override: bool = False,
    reason: str | None = None,
    can_override: bool = False,
) -> bool

    Apply an override request to a gate decision; return whether it was overridden.

    Raises PROMOTION_BLOCKED (blocked: no override possible), OVERRIDE_REQUIRED (needs an override that was not requested), FORBIDDEN (the caller may not override: manage on the endpoint, a signed-in admin) or SCHEMA_INVALID (an override without a reason). The caller audits an override as endpoint.promote_override.

    What-if scenarios v0.4¶

    Precomputed UI views: small JSON documents the runner writes next to datasets and bundles and the browser reads through signed URLs (the control plane never decodes them).

    Every view carries a format tag so readers can refuse versions they do not understand:

    ===================== ======================== ========================================== file format content ===================== ======================== ========================================== preview.json mapi.preview/v1 a long-format sample: dim then var columns profile.json mapi.profile/v1 per-variable statistics + missingness grid ui/tree_index.json mapi.tree-index/v1 structure of the bundle DataTree (no arrays) ui/preprocess.json mapi.preprocess/v1 learned preprocessing state per pipeline step ui/grids/mapi.response-grid/v1per-draw response curves for what-if sliders response_curves.json (M3; :class:ResponseGridView) ui/guided/mapi.forecast/v1a forecast score run's KPI: history, then the forecast.json forecast fan after the split (M3) ui/guided/mapi.counterfactual/v1a counterfactual score run's change of the counterfactual.json KPI, in total and per period (M3) ui/explore/mapi.model-explorer. quantised posterior rasters of the outputs fields.jsonfields/v1 that declare a grid (:class:FieldsView) ===================== ======================== ==========================================

    Views are produced inside the sandbox from untrusted data: strings are capped and readers must render them as text only.

    ResponseGridView ¶

    Bases: _View

    ui/grids/response_curves.json: per-draw response curves for instant what-if sliders.

    For each thinned posterior draw d, channel c and spend multiplier m, contribution[d][c][m] is the channel's total contribution to the KPI over the fit window (periods periods, KPI units) when the channel's spend is scaled by multipliers[m]; spend[c][m] is that spend (spend units). Multiplier 1 is the actual spend (current_spend). baseline[d] is the KPI over the window that no channel explains, so baseline[d] + sum_c contribution[d][c][at 1] is the model's expected KPI. *_by_geo variants add a trailing geo axis (geos order).

    Sliders interpolate per draw (see :func:mapi_spec.whatif.evaluate_scenario), so uncertainty bands stay joint across channels; "Run exact" submits a real score run.

    What-if scenarios, forecasts and counterfactuals for Guided mode (plan §11 tasks 6-7; M3).

    Sliders. A :class:WhatIfScenario scales each channel's spend over the fit window. The browser answers it instantly from the fit's :class:~mapi_spec.views.ResponseGridView with the interpolation contract below; :func:evaluate_scenario is the reference implementation (the web app's TypeScript port is tested against the same golden cases):

    1. a channel without a multiplier keeps 1; multipliers outside the grid ([multipliers[0], multipliers[-1]]) are refused (SCENARIO_OUT_OF_RANGE) - the grid is never extrapolated;
    2. per draw d and channel c, the contribution at multiplier x is the linear interpolation of contribution[d][c] between the two grid points around x; spend is interpolated the same way on spend[c];
    3. per draw, kpi = baseline + sum_c contribution and delta = kpi - kpi(all at 1); summaries (mean and quantiles) are taken over draws after summing, so uncertainty stays joint across channels.

    Run exact turns the scenario into a counterfactual :class:~mapi_spec.spec.ScoreRequest (:func:scenario_score_request). Forecasts (:func:forecast_request) and intervention presets ("channel off", "budget x k"; :func:counterfactual_request) build score requests the same way, so the server, the CLI and the docs share one implementation (POST /v1/guided/requests:compile).

    WhatIfScenario ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Spend multipliers per channel over the fit window (1 = what was actually spent).

    geo restricts the scenario to one geo's grid (needs a per-geo grid).

    WhatIfResult ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    The scenario's outcome over the fit window, in the grid's units.

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Mean and quantiles over posterior draws (quantiles[i] at levels[i]).

    Intervention preset: what if this channel had spent nothing?

    Endpoints and snippets v0.4¶

    See Integrations.

    Endpoints: stable aliases for promoted model versions (plan §2, §8.2, §11; Q13; M3).

    An endpoint endpoint://<project>/<alias> points at one model version at a time. Integrations (the Python and TypeScript clients, Google Sheets, BI exports) call the alias, so a new model version can be promoted - or rolled back - without touching them.

    • Promotion (PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias}) passes the promotion gate (:func:mapi_spec.scorecard.promotion_gate): the scorecard, the endpoint's :class:EvaluationPolicy (evaluate_then_refit by default, Q13) and the input-schema compatibility with what callers already send (:func:schema_breaks).
    • Every promotion and rollback is an :class:EndpointRevision (the history).
    • Scoring (POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score) takes an :class:EndpointScoreCall: a score request without apiVersion/kind/model, whose data and scenario may be dataset references or small inline XrJSON datasets.
    • GET …/schema describes the input (:class:EndpointSchema, with an example payload), POST …/validate checks a call without running it, GET …/snippets returns code (:mod:mapi_spec.snippets).

    Endpoint ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A stable alias and the model version it serves now.

    EvaluationPolicy ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    What a model version must satisfy to be promoted to the endpoint (Q13).

    fit_mode = evaluate_then_refit (default) requires versions whose production bundle was refitted on all data after the holdout evaluation; train_only also accepts exploration fits. schema_change decides what happens when the new version expects input the endpoint's callers do not send (:func:schema_breaks).

    EndpointSchemaSnapshot ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    The input contract of the promoted version, frozen at promotion: what callers send.

    input_schema is the schema at inputs_stage under the spec's canonical names (data.bind applied: time, y), which inline payloads use; the runner renames them to the dataset's own names before scoring. horizon_dim is the canonical name of the dim a forecast extends. conditions_on_actuals: forecasts can carry actuals (target values for periods after the fit) that the model updates its state with (:mod:mapi_spec.actuals); the server sets it from the capabilities of the plugin build that serves the endpoint now, not only from those at fit.

    EndpointPromote ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias}: create the alias or point it at another version.

    Name the version by id or by model://project/name@vN (exactly one). A version whose gate says needs_override needs override=true and a reason from a signed-in project admin (audited); blocked versions cannot be promoted. expected_revision guards against concurrent promotions (409 CONFLICT when stale).

    EndpointRevision ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    One entry of an endpoint's history (newest first in GET …/history).

    EndpointRollback ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/rollback: point the alias back at the version of an earlier revision (default: the one before the current). The gate is not re-run - the version was promoted before - but the rollback is audited with its reason. M3.5: when a governance policy requires validated models, the earlier version must still be validated (NOT_VALIDATED otherwise).

    EndpointScoreCall ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score (and …/validate): a score request for the endpoint's current version.

    data/scenario are dataset:// references or inline XrJSON datasets (up to 5 MB; :mod:mapi_spec.xrjson). Send Prefer: wait=N (N ≤ 60) to wait: 200 with the result when the run finishes in time, else 202 with the run.

    to_score_request ¶

    to_score_request(endpoint: str) -> ScoreRequest

    The :class:~mapi_spec.spec.ScoreRequest for endpoint (an endpoint:// ref). Inline datasets are left out: the server stores them as the run inputs :data:INPUT_INLINE_DATA / :data:INPUT_INLINE_SCENARIO.

    inline_inputs ¶

    inline_inputs() -> dict[str, XrJsonDataset]

    Inline payloads by run input name.

    EndpointSchema ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    GET /v1/endpoints/{alias}/schema: what to send, with a ready example payload.

    EndpointValidation ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/validate: the static checks of a score call (CoordPlan, capabilities, inline payload envelope) without running it.

    schema_breaks ¶

    schema_breaks(
    old: DataSchema, new: DataSchema
) -> list[str]

    Why callers that send data for old would break against new (plain text).

    Breaking: a dim that disappears or changes kind; a dim policy that no longer allows what it did (extend/new_levels → fixed); a new required input variable (not a target, missing values forbidden); an input variable whose dims or dtype family change. Dropped variables and loosened policies are compatible.

    example_score_call ¶

    example_score_call(
    snapshot: EndpointSchemaSnapshot, *, periods: int = 8
) -> EndpointScoreCall

    An example payload for an endpoint (shown by GET …/schema and the snippets).

    Forecasting endpoints get a forecast of periods that carries covariates forward (no inline data needed); others get a predict call with a one-cell-per-level inline dataset over the last fitted period, with placeholder zeros for every input variable. The summary is the model's representation default (mean/hdi_90 for draws, median/q5/q95 for quantile models, which have no mean), so the example scores.

    XrJSON: small labelled datasets inline in JSON requests (plan §3.2; M3 endpoints).

    The shape is xr.Dataset.to_dict()::

    {"coords": {"time": {"dims": ["time"], "data": ["2026-11-01", ...]}, ...},
 "data_vars": {"spend": {"dims": ["geo", "channel", "time"], "data": [[[...]]]}},
 "dims": {"time": 8, ...},           # optional
 "attrs": {}}                        # optional

    It is for payloads up to :data:MAX_XRJSON_BYTES (one scenario, an endpoint score call), so curl, TypeScript and Apps Script callers need no upload. The control plane checks only the envelope here (names, nesting, sizes, element and string caps, ragged lists) and stores the JSON as a run input; the values are decoded into arrays only inside the runner sandbox (mapi_sdk wire format), which also checks dtypes and the schema.

    XrJsonDataset ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    An inline dataset (xr.Dataset.to_dict() shape). Dim lengths must agree across variables; every dim of a data variable should have a coord (checked in the sandbox against the model's schema).

    XrJsonVariable ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    A coord or data variable: data nested len(dims) deep (a scalar for no dims).

    check_xrjson_size ¶

    check_xrjson_size(payload: Any) -> int

    Serialized size of an inline payload; raises PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE over :data:MAX_XRJSON_BYTES (check before model validation to bound the work).

    Code snippets for calling an endpoint (plan §11 Integrations hub; M3).

    Pure functions, so the server (GET /v1/endpoints/{alias}/snippets), the CLI and the docs render identical code. Every snippet scores POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score with Prefer: wait=60 and an example payload, reading the API token from the environment (MAPI_TOKEN; Apps Script: a script property) - a snippet never contains a secret.

    Actuals and future dates. With the endpoint's input table (:attr:SnippetContext.input_table, EndpointSchema.input_table) the Apps Script reads an "Input" sheet in that layout - actual rows with the target filled, rows to forecast with it blank, dates as yyyy-MM-dd - even when the example call sends no data, can create that sheet, and writes the forecast's conditioning note above the tables in "Result". The other snippets add a forecast over the table's rows (:attr:SnippetContext.table_call) to fill with actuals (:mod:mapi_spec.actuals).

    Quoting. Values are embedded with each language's own literal syntax, never by string pasting: Python literals via repr, JavaScript/TypeScript via JSON (with U+2028/U+2029 escaped), shell via single quotes (' → '\''), R via escaped single-quoted strings. The base URL, project and alias are validated first (:class:SnippetContext), so even a hostile value cannot break out of its literal; tests parse the generated code back.

    Webhooks v0.4¶

    Outgoing webhooks: events, envelope, signatures, deliveries and the SSRF policy (plan §8.2 Integrations, §9 "Webhook SSRF"; M3).

    Events (:class:WebhookEventType) are delivered as a JSON :class:WebhookEnvelope::

    {"id": "evt_…", "type": "run.succeeded", "created": "2026-10-15T09:30:00Z",
 "tenant": "acme", "project": "growth", "api_version": "v1", "data": {...}}

    Signatures. Every delivery carries Mapi-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex> where v1 is HMAC-SHA256 under the webhook secret of "<t>.<raw body>". While a secret is being rotated the header carries one v1 per active secret. Receivers verify with :func:verify_signature and refuse timestamps more than :data:SIGNATURE_TOLERANCE_S (300 s) away from their clock, which bounds replays.

    SSRF. The server delivers only under :data:SSRF_POLICY: https only, allowed ports, no credentials in URLs, blocked internal host names; it resolves the host itself, refuses if any address is private, loopback, link-local, metadata, CGNAT, ULA, multicast or otherwise non-global (:func:ip_is_blocked, including IPv4 embedded in IPv6), connects to the pinned address it checked (SNI and Host keep the name), follows no redirects, gives up after 5 s and reads at most 256 KiB of the response.

    SSRF_POLICY ¶

    SSRF_POLICY: Final = SsrfPolicy()

    WebhookEventType ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    Sent to the tenant's webhooks just before they are purged with everything else.

    The JSON body of every delivery. data depends on type:

    • run.*: {run_id, kind, state, failure_class?, code?, model_version_id?};
    • model.version.ready: {model_id, model_version_id, ref, scorecard_overall};
    • endpoint.promoted: {alias, ref, revision, model_version_id, overridden};
    • score.completed: {run_id, endpoint?, model_version_id, outputs: [names]};
    • tenant.deletion.completed: {deletion_id, requested_at, completed_at}.

    No envelope carries data values, signed URLs or secrets: fetch results with the API.

    error is platform-authored; response_excerpt is the first bytes of the receiver's answer (untrusted text: render as text only).

    check_signature ¶

    check_signature(
    body: bytes,
    header: str | None,
    secrets_: str | Iterable[str],
    *,
    now: int | None = None,
    tolerance: int = SIGNATURE_TOLERANCE_S,
) -> int

    Verify a delivery; return its timestamp or raise WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID.

    Accepts if any v1 matches any of secrets_ (constant-time comparison) and the timestamp is within tolerance seconds of now (either direction).

    next_retry_delay(
    attempt: int,
    response_code: int | None = None,
    *,
    jitter: float = 0.0,
) -> timedelta | None

    The delay before the next try after attempt failed, or None to give up.

    2xx is success (no retry); 410 Gone never retries; jitter in [0, 1) adds up to 10% (callers pass a random number; tests pass a fixed one).

    ip_is_blocked ¶

    ip_is_blocked(
    address: str | IPv4Address | IPv6Address,

    Is address unsafe to connect to? Covers every non-global range and IPv4 embedded in IPv6 (mapped ::ffff:a.b.c.d, NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, 6to4 2002::/16).

    check_webhook_url ¶

    check_webhook_url(
    url: str, policy: SsrfPolicy = SSRF_POLICY
) -> str

    Static checks of a webhook URL (before any DNS). Returns the lower-cased host.

    Raises WEBHOOK_URL_BLOCKED for: another scheme, credentials, a fragment, a port outside policy.ports, an IP literal, a blocked host name or suffix, a single-label host, or characters outside a plain DNS name.

    check_resolved_addresses ¶

    check_resolved_addresses(
    addresses: Sequence[str],
    policy: SsrfPolicy = SSRF_POLICY,
) -> str

    After resolution: every address must be allowed; return the one to pin (the first).

    Raises WEBHOOK_URL_BLOCKED when there is none or any is blocked (a host with one private and one public address is refused: DNS answers can rotate).

    Plot sharing v0.4¶

    Saved plots, static rendering and embeds (plan §8.2 Plots, §10.3 items 4-5; M3).

    • Saved plots (POST /v1/plots) keep a plot under a name: either a reference to a plot a model version rendered (a platform recipe or a plugin plot) or a user-authored :class:~mapi_spec.plots.PlotSpec (sanitized on save and on every read).
    • Static rendering (POST /v1/plots:render) turns a plot into PNG, SVG or PDF in the sandbox (vl-convert for Vega-Lite, kaleido for Plotly): a render run.
    • Embeds (POST /v1/plots/{plot_id}/embeds) mint a tokenised, read-only, expiring link for BI tools, Slack and Notion. Plan §10.3 item 4: shared views render platform recipes only - never plugin- or user-authored specs - because a sandboxed iframe can still navigate itself; :func:embeddable decides. The public GET /v1/embeds/{token} returns an :class:EmbedView with every dataset inlined (no URLs).

    Embed tokens are mpe_<40 base32 characters> (200 random bits); the server stores only an HMAC (like API tokens) and shows the URL once.

    SavedPlotCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /v1/plots: exactly one of source (a model version's plot) or spec (a user-authored plot, sanitized first; never embeddable).

    A plot a model version rendered (GET /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v}/plots).

Send Prefer: wait=N to get the file links in the response.

    Trust lifecycle v0.4¶

    Trust lifecycle: self-service sign-up, verification, tenant deletion and GDPR export (plan §9 "Compute abuse", "Data lifecycle", §14 M3 and cut lines A/B; M3).

    • Sign-up (POST /auth/signup): e-mail, name and accepted terms. The answer is the same whether or not the address is new (no account enumeration). A disposable-e-mail policy hook (:class:DisposableEmailPolicy) refuses throwaway domains.
    • E-mail verification (POST /auth/verify-email) with a single-use token that expires after :data:EMAIL_VERIFICATION_TTL creates a public-tier tenant with a default project, the signer as tenant admin.
    • Cut line A (M3): public tenants run declarative specs and built-in plugins only - untrusted data, trusted code. Cut line B (M5) opens code upload to public tenants, and only after identity verification (:func:uploaded_code_allowed).
    • Tenant deletion (POST /v1/tenants/{id}/deletion) is scheduled with a grace period (:data:TENANT_DELETION_GRACE, the tenant is suspended and can cancel), then purges every store and reports progress per store (:class:TenantDeletion).
    • GDPR export (POST /v1/tenants/{id}/exports) packages everything the tenant stored into one archive with a short-lived download link (:class:GdprExport).

    About cards and the chooser v0.5¶

    See About cards and choosing.

    Plain-language "About" cards and the "Help me choose" chooser (M3.5).

    Every item a user picks from a catalog - models, preprocessing steps and splits, guided templates and specs, workflow templates, workflow node kinds and node implementations, governance checks, datasets - carries an :class:About: what it is in one or two sentences without jargon, when to use it and when not to, the data it needs, what it assumes, what you get out, how hard it is, how long it usually takes, a tiny example and related items. Expert detail (maths, references) lives apart in expert_notes and references.

    • :func:about_issues is the completeness rule the catalog and the contract kit apply (mapi_spec.catalog.catalog_about_issues, mapi_sdk.testing.check_about);
    • :class:DatasetAbout combines a user's description of a dataset with a summary generated from its schema and coordinate summary (:func:describe_dataset, pure);
    • the chooser asks :data:CHOOSER_QUESTIONS and ranks candidates by their :attr:About.fits tags (:func:recommend, pure), behind GET /v1/catalog/chooser and GET /v1/catalog/recommendations.

    Pure Pydantic and stdlib (no numpy): the control plane, the web app and the docs share it.

) -> ChooserResult

    Rank candidates ((kind, id, About)) against answers (pure, deterministic).

    Each answered question an item declares in :attr:About.fits adds the question's weight when an answer matches (a reason) or subtracts it when none does (a caution); undeclared questions are neutral. experience below the item's difficulty and speed below its typical runtime cost one point per level. Scores are normalised to [0, 1]; ties break by the number of answers an item matches explicitly (an item made for every answer before one that is silent on some), then difficulty, then id.

    When goal is answered, an item made for other goals is never recommended (items whose goal does not match are dropped). When no candidate matches the goal, fallback (other kinds: the building blocks behind the starting points) is ranked instead.

    About cards of the built-in catalog (M3.5): steps, splits, models and guided templates.

    The text is written for people who do not do statistics for a living: the summary says what the item does for them, the lists say when it fits, what it needs and what comes out, and expert_notes keeps the maths apart. Workflow nodes and governance checks keep their cards next to their registries (:mod:mapi_spec.workflow_nodes, :mod:mapi_spec.governance); :func:builtin_about looks up any of them by id.

    Built-in steps and models take their card from here when their class does not set one (mapi_sdk.steps.Step.about, mapi_sdk.models.CustomModel.about). Models that are built in other v0.5 components (mmm-framework and statsmodels) are listed too, so their plugins and the chooser agree on the words: :data:PLANNED_MODEL_IDS.

    Workflows v0.5¶

    See Workflows.

    Workflows: versioned DAGs of statistical tests, data processing and models (M3.5).

    A :class:WorkflowSpec (kind: Workflow, YAML or JSON like every spec document) nests tests, transforms, branches, splits, searches, model fits, evaluations, comparisons, selections, governance checks, reports and sub-workflows into one automated pipeline::

    apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata: {name: ts-readiness, project: growth}
params:
  alpha: {type: number, default: 0.05}
inputs:
  data: {type: dataset}
nodes:
  - {id: adf, use: test.adf, inputs: {data: inputs.data}, with: {alpha: {$param: alpha}}}
  - {id: kpss, use: test.kpss, inputs: {data: inputs.data}}
  - id: wanders
    use: branch.if
    with: {condition: "nodes.adf.p_value >= params.alpha or nodes.kpss.reject"}
  - {id: diff, use: transform.difference, inputs: {data: inputs.data}, when: wanders.then}
  - id: order
    use: search.arma_order
    inputs: {data: [diff.data, inputs.data]}     # first available: diff ran, or not
outputs: {order: order.table}

    Wiring. An input port binds inputs.<name> or <node>.<port>. For a single-value port a list binds alternatives, the first whose node ran (a node gated by a branch arm that was not taken is skipped, and so are its dependants unless they have an alternative); for a multiple port (PortSpec.multiple) a list binds every source that ran. A node whose required port has no available binding is skipped. when: <branch>.then|else gates a node on a branch. Parameters (with) may be literals, {$param: name} (a workflow parameter) or {$expr: "..."} (a value computed from upstream results with the safe expression language, :mod:mapi_spec.expr).

    Static validation (:func:validate_workflow, synchronous, JSON only) reports every problem as an :class:~mapi_spec.errors.Issue with a JSON pointer: unknown node implementations, parameter schema violations and missing parameters, unbound required ports, port-type mismatches, references to unknown nodes, ports or parameters, branch conditions that do not parse or read fields their node does not produce, cycles, nodes that can never run (gated by both arms of one branch) and unused results.

    Runs. POST /v1/workflows/{id}/runs starts a workflow run (a parent run). The orchestrator walks the DAG in topological order, evaluates branches itself, sends sandbox nodes to workflow_node runs and child_run nodes to ordinary runs (fits), reuses unchanged results by :func:node_cache_key, retries per node, and records a :class:NodeRun per node and a :class:BranchDecision per branch.

    WorkflowSpec ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    The declarative workflow document (kind: Workflow).

    WorkflowNode ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    One node: an implementation (use), its parameters and its wiring.

    WorkflowParam ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A run-time parameter (params.<name> in conditions, {$param: name} in nodes).

    WorkflowInput ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A workflow input (inputs.<name>): a dataset, a model version, a split plan...

    WorkflowExecution ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Run-wide settings.

    WorkflowValidation ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    POST /v1/workflows:validate: issues located by JSON pointers, the execution order and the resolved implementation of every node.

    Workflow ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    A saved workflow (workflow://project/name) and its latest revision.

    WorkflowCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /v1/workflows: a workflow with its first revision (the document).

    WorkflowUpdate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    PATCH /v1/workflows/{workflow_id}: metadata only (documents are revisions).

    WorkflowRevision ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    An immutable, hashed revision; validation is its static check at save time (revisions with errors are stored but cannot run: WORKFLOW_NOT_RUNNABLE).

    WorkflowRevisionCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /v1/workflows/{workflow_id}/revisions.

    WorkflowValidateRequest ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /v1/workflows:validate (sync, stores nothing).

    WorkflowRunCreate ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST /v1/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs (Idempotency-Key).

    WorkflowRun ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    GET /v1/workflow-runs/{run_id}: a run of a workflow revision with every node.

    WorkflowRunStatus ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    NodeRun ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    One node of a workflow run.

    NodeRunStatus ¶

    Bases: StrEnum

    CACHED ¶

    CACHED = 'cached'

    Succeeded by reusing an earlier result with the same cache key.

    SKIPPED ¶

    SKIPPED = 'skipped'

    Gated by a branch arm that was not taken, or every alternative input was skipped.

    produced ¶

    produced: bool

    The node has outputs (dependants may bind them).

    NodeOutputRef ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Where a node output lives: a reference (dataset://, model://), a run artifact (run_id + object) or, for small JSON payloads (test results, split plans, metrics), inline.

    NodeError ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    BranchDecision ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    Why a branch went one way: the condition, its value and the values it read.

    The safe condition language of workflow branches (M3.5).

    Branch nodes decide which way a workflow goes from the results of upstream nodes, e.g. nodes.adf.p_value < params.alpha and not nodes.kpss.reject. Conditions are parsed by a small hand-written tokenizer and recursive-descent parser into an immutable AST and evaluated by walking it over plain JSON data. Nothing is ever passed to eval/exec, no attribute of a Python object is ever read (references index dicts and lists only), and every input is bounded (:data:LIMITS), so a hostile condition can at worst be refused.

    Grammar (EBNF; keywords are lowercase, whitespace is insignificant)::

    expression  = or ;
or          = and , { "or" , and } ;
and         = not , { "and" , not } ;
not         = "not" , not | comparison ;
comparison  = sum , [ compare_op , sum ] ;        (* no chaining: a < b < c is refused *)
compare_op  = "==" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" | "in" | "not" , "in" ;
sum         = product , { ( "+" | "-" ) , product } ;
product     = unary , { ( "*" | "/" | "%" ) , unary } ;
unary       = "-" , unary | primary ;
primary     = number | string | "true" | "false" | "null" | list | call | reference
            | "(" , expression , ")" ;
list        = "[" , [ expression , { "," , expression } ] , "]" ;
call        = function , "(" , [ expression , { "," , expression } ] , ")" ;
function    = "abs" | "min" | "max" | "len" | "round" | "any" | "all" | "exists"
            | "coalesce" | "if" ;
reference   = root , { "." , name | "[" , ( integer | string ) , "]" } ;
root        = "nodes" | "params" | "inputs" | "run" ;
number      = digit , { digit } , [ "." , digit , { digit } ] , [ exponent ] ;
string      = "'" , { character } , "'" | '"' , { character } , '"' ;

    Semantics are strict so conditions mean what they say: and/or/not need booleans (no truthiness), ordering compares numbers with numbers and strings with strings, == compares any JSON values (1 == 1.0; true != 1), in tests list membership or a substring, arithmetic is on numbers only, and a missing reference is an error unless it is wrapped in exists(...) or coalesce(...). and/or short-circuit, and so does if(condition, a, b) (only the chosen value is evaluated), which turns a decision into a value: if(nodes.wanders.value, 1, 0).

    Five-field cron expressions for workflow schedules (M3.5; pure stdlib).

    minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week with *, numbers, ranges a-b, steps */n and a-b/n, lists a,b,c and the names jan-dec / sun-sat (Sunday is 0 or 7). As in Vixie cron, when both day fields are restricted a day matches if either matches. Macros: @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly, @yearly.

    :func:next_fire computes the next time strictly after a given instant in an IANA time zone (zoneinfo); a local time skipped by a daylight-saving jump does not fire, a repeated one fires once. Schedules may not fire more often than every :data:MIN_INTERVAL_MINUTES minutes (checked by :func:check_cron).

    The tightest schedule allowed (workflows spend compute unattended).

    Split plans and test results v0.5¶

    Split plans: multi-fold train/test designs for workflows and backtests (M3.5).

    A ModelSpec holds one train/holdout :data:~mapi_spec.spec.Split (data.split). A :data:SplitPlan describes many folds - a backtest - and is what workflow split nodes produce (port type split_plan) and model/evaluate nodes consume:

    ==================== ====================================================================== kind folds ==================== ====================================================================== holdout one fold: an existing Split (time_holdout, as_of, ...) rolling_origin a fixed-length training window that slides forward; test windows of max(horizons) periods after an optional gap expanding_window like rolling origin, but training always starts at the beginning blocked_kfold k contiguous blocks; each is the test once, with gap periods left out of training on both sides purged_kfold blocked k-fold with purge periods before and embargo after each test block dropped from training (overlapping labels) geo_holdout whole groups (geos, stores) held out, optionally only over the last test_last periods; repeated over seeded random draws nested an inner plan run inside every training window of an outer plan (tune on inner folds, score on outer ones) ==================== ======================================================================

    Folds are computed from metadata only (:func:plan_folds for ordered plans, from the number of positions along dim; :func:plan_group_folds for group plans, from the levels), so the control plane can show them before anything runs. Positions are 0-based half-open windows [start, stop). expanding_window and rolling_origin match scikit-learn's TimeSeriesSplit (test_size=max(horizons), gap, max_train_size) when step == max(horizons) and anchor="end"; blocked_kfold with gap=0 matches KFold(shuffle=False). An expanding fold is exactly an as_of split (:meth:Fold.as_of_split), so the existing split machinery runs it.

    HoldoutPlan ¶

    Bases: _PlanBase

    One fold: the existing train/holdout split.

    RollingOriginPlan ¶

    Bases: _WindowPlan

    A fixed-length training window sliding forward.

    ExpandingWindowPlan ¶

    Bases: _WindowPlan

    Training from the first period up to each origin.

    BlockedKFoldPlan ¶

    Bases: _PlanBase

    k contiguous blocks; gap periods on each side of the test block are dropped.

    PurgedKFoldPlan ¶

    Bases: _PlanBase

    Blocked k-fold with purge periods before and embargo after each test block removed from training (labels that overlap the test window).

    GeoHoldoutPlan ¶

    Bases: _PlanBase

    Hold out whole groups along dim: the explicit groups (one fold), or n seeded random groups in each of n_folds folds. With time_dim/test_last, the held-out groups are tested on their last periods only, and include_pre_period trains on their earlier periods too (a geo experiment readout).

    NestedPlan ¶

    Bases: _PlanBase

    An inner plan inside every training window of an outer ordered plan.

    Fold ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    One fold. Ordered plans fill the position windows; group plans fill the groups.

    excluded are extra windows left out of training (gaps, purges, embargoes); the first gap positions of the test window's lead are scored for continuity only when the plan says so (as_of semantics), never counted in metrics.

    train_positions ¶

    train_positions: list[int]

    Training positions (ordered folds), with excluded windows removed.

    as_of_split ¶

    as_of_split(dim: str, coords: list[Scalar]) -> AsOfSplit

    The existing as_of split this expanding fold stands for (train_start must be 0): train up to and including coords[train_stop - 1], skip the gap.

    plan_folds ¶

    plan_folds(
    plan: HoldoutPlan | OrderedPlan | NestedPlan, n: int
) -> list[Fold]

    Folds of an ordered plan over n positions along its dim (pure).

    k-fold folds train on [0, n) minus excluded (which includes the test block); window folds train on [train_start, train_stop). holdout plans need the data to resolve their split and are refused here (SPLIT_INVALID); so are group plans (:func:plan_group_folds). Raises SPLIT_INVALID when the data is too short.

    plan_group_folds ¶

    plan_group_folds(
    plan: GeoHoldoutPlan,
    levels: list[Scalar],
    *,
    n_time: int | None = None,
) -> list[Fold]

    Folds of a geo_holdout plan over the group levels (pure, seeded).

    With test_last, n_time (positions along time_dim) is required and every fold tests its groups on [n_time - test_last, n_time); include_pre_period trains on their earlier periods too.

    Statistical test results: the test_result payload of workflow test nodes and the rows of the Data Explorer's stationarity table (M3.5).

    The runner computes tests with statsmodels/scipy in the sandbox; this module fixes what a result looks like and how a p-value becomes a decision, so the control plane (branch conditions), the web app and the docs agree. Every test states its null hypothesis and both possible verdicts in plain words (:data:TEST_DEFINITIONS); :func:decide applies the significance level, including for tests whose null is the "good" case (KPSS: the series is stationary).

    Governance v0.5¶

    See Governance.

    Model governance: policies, the check catalog, evidence, the validation state machine, approvals and the evidence pack (M3.5).

    A :class:GovernancePolicy (tenant- or project-scoped, versioned) lists the checks a model of a family must pass before it is validated, with thresholds and severities, and whether a second person must approve. Checks run as governance workflows in the sandbox (governance.policy nodes); their :class:CheckResult s with :class:EvidenceItem s are stored on a :class:ModelValidation.

    Validation status (:func:transition, pure and exhaustive)::

    draft             --submit-->           checks_running
checks_running    --checks_passed-->    checks_passed
checks_running    --checks_failed-->    checks_failed
checks_running    --cancel-->           draft
checks_passed     --validate-->         validated          (no approval required)
checks_passed     --request_approval--> awaiting_approval  (approval required)
awaiting_approval --approve-->          validated
awaiting_approval --reject-->           rejected
checks_failed     --resubmit-->         checks_running
checks_failed     --reject-->           rejected
rejected          --resubmit-->         checks_running
validated         --deprecate-->        deprecated

    Approvals need a reviewer who is not the submitter (:func:check_approver). When a policy says require_validated_for_promotion, promoting a model version to an endpoint needs status validated (:func:mapi_spec.scorecard.promotion_gate, reason NOT_VALIDATED). Every transition is audited and emitted as a webhook event.

    GOVERNANCE_CHECKS ¶

    GOVERNANCE_CHECKS: Final[dict[str, GovernanceCheckDef]] = {
    c.id: c for c in _CHECKS
}

    The governance check catalog by id.

    TRANSITIONS ¶

    TRANSITIONS: Final[
    dict[
        tuple[ValidationStatus, ValidationEvent],
        ValidationStatus,
    ]
] = {
    (_S.DRAFT, _EV.SUBMIT): _S.CHECKS_RUNNING,
    (
        _S.CHECKS_RUNNING,
        _EV.CHECKS_PASSED,
    ): _S.CHECKS_PASSED,
    (
        _S.CHECKS_RUNNING,
        _EV.CHECKS_FAILED,
    ): _S.CHECKS_FAILED,
    (_S.CHECKS_RUNNING, _EV.CANCEL): _S.DRAFT,
    (
        _S.CHECKS_PASSED,
        _EV.REQUEST_APPROVAL,
    ): _S.AWAITING_APPROVAL,
    (_S.CHECKS_PASSED, _EV.VALIDATE): _S.VALIDATED,
    (_S.CHECKS_FAILED, _EV.RESUBMIT): _S.CHECKS_RUNNING,
    (_S.CHECKS_FAILED, _EV.REJECT): _S.REJECTED,
    (_S.AWAITING_APPROVAL, _EV.APPROVE): _S.VALIDATED,
    (_S.AWAITING_APPROVAL, _EV.REJECT): _S.REJECTED,
    (_S.REJECTED, _EV.RESUBMIT): _S.CHECKS_RUNNING,
    (_S.VALIDATED, _EV.DEPRECATE): _S.DEPRECATED,
}

    Explorers and budget optimisation v0.5¶

    Requests for the Data Explorer and the Model Explorer (M3.5).

    POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions/{version}/explore (a :class:DataExploreRequest) and POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/explore (a :class:ModelExploreRequest) start an explore run: the sandbox decodes the data (or the bundle), computes the requested sections and writes the views of :mod:mapi_spec.views under ui/explore/. Results are cached per (target, request hash), so asking again is instant. :class:ExploreJob is the run's RunSpec.spec.

    DataExploreRequest ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Which Data Explorer sections to compute, and how.

    kpi is the result the cross-correlations are computed against (default: the dataset's target variable); facet_by splits series by up to two dims; period is the season length for STL and seasonal strength (default: from the frequency).

    ModelExploreRequest ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    Which Model Explorer sections to compute. compare_with adds other model versions (model://…) to the comparison section; backtest runs a split plan for the backtest section (fits run as child runs).

    ExploreJob ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    RunSpec.spec of an explore run. Inputs: dataset (and schema) for a dataset; bundle and bundle.manifest (plus compare.<k> bundles) for a model.

    Precomputed UI views: small JSON documents the runner writes next to datasets and bundles and the browser reads through signed URLs (the control plane never decodes them).

    Every view carries a format tag so readers can refuse versions they do not understand:

    ===================== ======================== ========================================== file format content ===================== ======================== ========================================== preview.json mapi.preview/v1 a long-format sample: dim then var columns profile.json mapi.profile/v1 per-variable statistics + missingness grid ui/tree_index.json mapi.tree-index/v1 structure of the bundle DataTree (no arrays) ui/preprocess.json mapi.preprocess/v1 learned preprocessing state per pipeline step ui/grids/mapi.response-grid/v1per-draw response curves for what-if sliders response_curves.json (M3; :class:ResponseGridView) ui/guided/mapi.forecast/v1a forecast score run's KPI: history, then the forecast.json forecast fan after the split (M3) ui/guided/mapi.counterfactual/v1a counterfactual score run's change of the counterfactual.json KPI, in total and per period (M3) ui/explore/mapi.model-explorer. quantised posterior rasters of the outputs fields.jsonfields/v1 that declare a grid (:class:FieldsView) ===================== ======================== ==========================================

    Views are produced inside the sandbox from untrusted data: strings are capped and readers must render them as text only.

    ExplorerIndex ¶

    Bases: _View

    ui/explore/index.json: what an explore run produced (and why a section is missing).

    ExplorerSectionRef ¶

    Bases: _View

    Bases: _Explore

    overview: shape, dims, variables and a plain-language summary.

    DistributionsView ¶

    distributions: a histogram and summary statistics per variable.

    MissingnessView ¶

    ParamTableView ¶

    ModelDiagnosticsView ¶

    FitVsActualView ¶

    fit: actual vs fitted with an interval, the split line at split_at.

    ResidualDiagnosticsView ¶

    Bases: _Explore

    residuals: residuals over time, their ACF, Ljung-Box, normality and spread tests.

    DecompositionView ¶

    Bases: _Explore

    decomposition: additive components over time and their share of the total.

    ResponseCurvesView ¶

    Bases: _Explore

    response_curves: mean response per channel with a band ([channel][point]; the full per-draw grid is :class:ResponseGridView).

    IrfView ¶

    Bases: _Explore

    irf: impulse responses of VAR/VECM models: values[i][j][h] is the response of variables[i] to a shock in variables[j] after h periods (h = 0..horizons).

    FevdView ¶

    Bases: _Explore

    fevd: forecast-error variance decomposition: shares[i][h][j] is the share of variables[i]'s forecast-error variance at horizon h + 1 due to variables[j].

    FieldsView ¶

    Bases: _Explore

    fields: the outputs that declare a grid as interactive rasters (intensity maps, images, space-time densities, vector fields), from the in-sample predictions.

    Rasters are quantised to uint16 (:class:FieldRaster); one view holds at most :data:MAX_FIELD_CELLS cells. omitted lists the grid outputs that are not shown (more than :data:MAX_FIELDS, or not in the predictions).

    FieldEntry ¶

    Bases: _View

    One output drawn as a 2-D field (see :class:mapi_spec.capabilities.GridDecl).

    y_coords/x_coords label the raster rows and columns (for a downsampled raster, the coordinate at the middle of each block). Row 0 is drawn at the top unless origin is lower. facet names the level of each other dim of the output (one entry per level). kind is vector when the output has a component dim.

    FieldFrame ¶

    Bases: _View

    One frame of a field (one level of its frame dim, or the only frame): the posterior mean, sd, 5% and 95% quantiles and a few draws, each a :class:FieldRaster. For a vector field the rasters are of the magnitude sqrt(u**2 + v**2) (per draw, then summarised) and arrows holds the mean components.

    FieldRaster ¶

    Bases: _View

    One quantised raster: height x width cells, row-major (row 0 first).

    data is the base64 of little-endian uint16 codes, two bytes per cell. Code :data:FIELD_NAN (65535) is a missing cell; a code q in 0..FIELD_LEVELS decodes to lo + (hi - lo) * q / FIELD_LEVELS (every code is lo when lo == hi). When the field's encoding is log10 that number is log10 of the value (values <= 0 are missing). lo/hi are None only when every cell is missing. The step between two codes is (hi - lo) / 65534: four to five significant digits.

    cells ¶

    cells() -> int

    The number of cells data holds (it must be valid base64 of whole uint16s).

    FieldArrows ¶

    Bases: _View

    The mean (x, y) components of a vector field on a coarse grid (one arrow per cell).

    x/y are the arrow centres in raster pixel units (column, row; fractional, 0 = the centre of the first pixel). u is the component along increasing column index and v along increasing row index (so with origin="lower" a positive v points up), both [row][col] in the field's units.

    ModelForecastView ¶

    Bases: _Explore

    forecast: forecast fans after the fitted history (see :class:ForecastView).

    BacktestView ¶

    Bases: _Explore

    backtest: metrics per fold and horizon for the model and its benchmarks.

    ComparisonView ¶

    Bases: _Explore

    comparison: several model versions side by side (table[model][metric]).

    explore_view_name ¶

    explore_view_name(section: str) -> str

    ui/explore/<section>.json: where an explore run writes a section.

    decode_raster ¶

    decode_raster(
    r: FieldRaster,
    encoding: Literal["linear", "log10"] = "linear",
) -> list[float | None]

    The values of a raster (row-major, None = missing), as a reader decodes them.

    Budget optimisation: POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}:optimize (plan §8.2; M3.5), backed by mmm-framework's planning module in the sandbox.

    An :class:OptimizeRequest asks how to split a budget across channels (and optionally geos): a total budget (or a change in percent of current spend, or mode="free" to fund every channel up to break-even), bounds per channel as multiples of current spend or in money, portfolio groups ("digital at least 40%"), the objective (the expected KPI, a cautious percentile such as p10, or the mean of the worst draws cvar5), a horizon and an optional efficient frontier. The optimize run answers with an :class:OptimizeResult: the allocation per channel [and geo] with the expected KPI and its interval, the uplift over the current plan with the chance it is positive, the expected regret of committing to one plan, the marginal return of every channel at the plan, and frontier points. Everything is computed from posterior draws in the sandbox; the control plane validates only the JSON.

    Mapping onto mmm-framework (planning.budget.optimize_budget, planning.frontier .budget_frontier, optimize_budget_by_geo): total_budget / budget_change_pct / mode / objective / value_per_kpi map one to one; ChannelBounds.min_multiplier / max_multiplier are its bounds and min_spend / max_spend its abs_bounds; groups its portfolio constraints; max_draws, n_steps and seed its sampling controls.

    OptimizeRequest ¶

    Bases: RequestModel

    POST …:optimize: how should the budget be split?

    objective: mean (expected KPI), p<q> (the q-th percentile across posterior draws, a cautious plan) or cvar<a> (mean of the worst a% of draws). mode: fixed spends the budget; free funds each channel to break-even (marginal value = 1 per unit of money, with value_per_kpi converting KPI to money) and makes the total an output. horizon is the number of future periods the plan covers (default: the fit window's length, as the response grid).

    ChannelBounds ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Bounds on one channel: as multiples of its current spend and/or in money (money bounds override multiples, as in mmm-framework).

    SpendGroup ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    A portfolio constraint over several channels (shares of the total and/or money).

    FrontierRequest ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    Also sweep budgets from budget_min to budget_max (default 40%-200% of the current total) in n_points steps.

    OptimizeResult ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    optimize.json: the recommended plan and its uncertainty.

    ChannelAllocation ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    The plan for one channel (and geo): spend now and at the optimum, shares, the expected contribution, the marginal return at the plan and how stable the recommendation is across draws.

    FrontierPoint ¶

    Bases: ResponseModel

    The best plan at one total budget.

    OptimizeJob ¶

    Bases: StrictModel

    RunSpec.spec of an optimize run (inputs: bundle, bundle.manifest).

    check_feasible ¶

    check_feasible(
    req: OptimizeRequest,
    current: dict[str, float],
    *,
    total: float | None = None,
) -> None

    Static feasibility from the current spend per channel (OPTIMIZE_INFEASIBLE): unknown channels, bounds whose minimums exceed the budget or whose maximums cannot reach it, and group shares that cannot be met together.

    Local development¶

    Local development topology: ports, origins and environment variable names.

    One place for the defaults every M1 component (API, GCS shim, runner, local executor, web app, plot sandbox) agrees on, so they can be started independently without drift. Every value can be overridden through the environment variable named next to it.

    LocalDev ¶

    LocalDev(
    env: str = DEFAULT_ENV,
    database_url: str | None = None,
    gcs_endpoint: str = f"http://{LOCALHOST}:{GCS_SHIM_PORT}",
    api_url: str = f"http://{LOCALHOST}:{API_PORT}",
    web_origin: str = f"http://{LOCALHOST}:{WEB_PORT}",
    plots_origin: str = f"http://{LOCALHOST}:{PLOT_SANDBOX_PORT}",
    data_dir: str = ".local",
)

    Resolved local configuration. database_url=None means "start embedded pgserver".

    from_environ ¶

    from_environ(environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> LocalDev

    Defaults overridden by any of the ENV_* variables that are set and non-empty.

    bootstrap_url_template ¶

    bootstrap_url_template() -> str

    MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL for executions talking to the local GCS shim.

    JSON Schema export¶

    Export JSON Schemas (2020-12) for every public document and contract model.

    GET /schemas/modelspec.json serves :func:export_schemas output; Monaco and JSON Forms use it, and CI snapshots it to detect drift.

    export_schemas ¶

    export_schemas(
    out_dir: str | Path | None = None,
) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]

    Return {filename: JSON Schema}; also write the files if out_dir is given.
